questions.question: Which colour traffic light means STOP?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which colour traffic light means STOP?
questions.context: Pictures: a red circle, a green circle, a yellow circle, a blue circle.
questions.expected: Red
questions.memo: Red = stop. Green = go (but still check). Yellow/amber = slow down, the light is about to change.

questions.question: A zebra crossing is:
questions.ruby_prompt: A zebra crossing on the road — what is it for?
options: A safe place for people to cross the road
A place for cars to park
A place for taxis to wait
questions.expected: A safe place for people to cross the road
questions.memo: Black-and-white stripes painted on the road. Cars are supposed to stop for people crossing — but you must still check before stepping in.

questions.question: When you are in a car, you should always wear:
questions.ruby_prompt: When you sit in a car, you should always wear what?
questions.expected: A seatbelt
questions.memo: Seatbelts save lives in a crash. In SA, the law requires everyone to belt up — front and back seats.

questions.question: When riding a bicycle, you should wear:
questions.ruby_prompt: When you ride a bicycle, what should you wear?
questions.context: Pictures: a helmet, slippers, a long dress, sunglasses.
questions.expected: A helmet
questions.memo: A helmet protects your head if you fall. Bright clothes help cars see you. Lights at night are also important.

questions.question: Which side of the road do pedestrians walk on if there is no pavement?
questions.ruby_prompt: If there is no pavement, which side of the road do you walk on in South Africa?
options: Facing oncoming traffic (the right-hand side as you walk)
In the middle of the road
questions.expected: Facing oncoming traffic (the right-hand side as you walk)
questions.memo: Facing traffic lets you see cars coming and step aside if needed. SA drives on the LEFT, so walking on the RIGHT means you face them.

questions.question: True or false: It is safe to play on or near railway tracks.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It is safe to play on or near railway tracks.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Never play on or near railway tracks. Trains can't stop quickly. Many children are killed or seriously injured on tracks every year in SA.

questions.question: What should you do at a railway level crossing?
questions.ruby_prompt: What should you do at a railway level crossing?
options: Stop, look both ways, and only cross when no train is coming
questions.expected: Stop, look both ways, and only cross when no train is coming
questions.memo: Trains move much faster than they look. Stop, look both ways, listen — only cross when you can see clearly that no train is coming.

questions.question: A red triangle road sign usually means:
questions.ruby_prompt: A red triangle on a road sign usually means what?
questions.expected: Warning — be careful
questions.memo: A red triangle sign is a warning. It tells people to be careful, maybe of a sharp bend or animals.

questions.question: When walking to school early in the morning or at dusk, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: When you walk to school early in the morning or in dim light, you should:
options: Wear bright or reflective clothes so drivers can see you
Walk in the middle of the road
questions.expected: Wear bright or reflective clothes so drivers can see you
questions.memo: Drivers can't avoid what they can't see. Bright colours, reflective strips, white items — all help cars see you in low light.

questions.question: Which is good behaviour in a taxi?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is good behaviour as a passenger in a taxi?
options: Sit still, don't distract the driver, wear a seatbelt if there is one
questions.expected: Sit still, don't distract the driver, wear a seatbelt if there is one
questions.memo: Sit still, don't distract the driver, and wear a seatbelt if there is one. A focused driver is safer.

questions.question: Cycling on a busy road, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: When cycling on a busy road, what should you do?
options: Ride in the same direction as traffic and use hand signals
Ride in the middle of the lane
questions.expected: Ride in the same direction as traffic and use hand signals
questions.memo: Cycle the same way as the cars. Stick to the side. Use hand signals when turning so drivers know what you're doing.

questions.question: What is a 'crosswalk' or 'pedestrian crossing' for?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a pedestrian crossing for?
options: Walking across the road in a safer place
questions.expected: Walking across the road in a safer place
questions.memo: A pedestrian crossing is a safer place to walk across the road. Cars should slow down and stop.

questions.question: Put these in the right order for crossing a road safely.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these steps in order for safely crossing a road.
options: Find a safe place to cross
Cross when clear, keep looking and listening
questions.expected: Find a safe place to cross,Stop at the edge,Look both ways and listen,Cross when clear, keep looking and listening
questions.memo: Safe spot, stop, look and listen, cross. The classic 'Green Cross Code' — saves lives everywhere.

questions.question: If you are too small to be seen behind a parked car, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you are too small to be seen behind a parked car, what should you do?
options: Cross away from parked cars, where drivers can see you
questions.expected: Cross away from parked cars, where drivers can see you
questions.memo: Parked cars hide you from drivers. Find an open spot to cross — somewhere drivers can actually see you coming.

questions.question: Mpho is walking on a busy road. A friend phones her. What should she do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho is walking on a busy road and her friend phones her. What should she do?
options: Step off the road into a safe spot before answering
Answer while walking with no looking
questions.expected: Step off the road into a safe spot before answering
questions.memo: Phones distract you. Step off the road first, talk in a safe place, then walk on. Most pedestrian accidents involve distraction.

questions.question: True or false: You should always sit in a vehicle with a seatbelt on.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: You should always sit with a seatbelt on in a vehicle.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Seatbelts halve your chance of being seriously injured in a crash. SA law requires belts when fitted.

questions.question: Tell me one road safety rule for pedestrians.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one road safety rule for pedestrians (people walking).
questions.expected: Stop, look both ways and listen before crossing
questions.memo: Stop, look both ways and listen before you cross. Use a crossing if there is one.

questions.question: Which is SAFER to do on a bakkie (pickup truck)?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is safer when you travel in a bakkie (pickup truck)?
options: Sit inside the cab with a seatbelt on
questions.expected: Sit inside the cab with a seatbelt on
questions.memo: Riding on the open back of a bakkie is dangerous — a sudden brake or turn can throw people out. Inside with a seatbelt is far safer.

questions.question: Why are railway tracks especially dangerous?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are railway tracks especially dangerous places?
options: Trains are heavy and fast and can't stop quickly
questions.expected: Trains are heavy and fast and can't stop quickly
questions.memo: A train takes hundreds of metres to stop. By the time the driver sees you, it's too late. Stay well clear of tracks — always.

LS.L4.PSW.T12.title: Personal and household hygiene
LS.L4.PSW.T12.description: Personal hygiene items that cannot be shared, germ breeding areas in the house.
LS.L4.PSW.T12.recovery_strategy: Keep tone matter-of-fact. Hygiene is a daily habit, not a punishment. Help the learner identify which items stay personal and which germs hide in.

questions.question: Which of these is a personal hygiene item that should NOT be shared?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a personal hygiene item that should NOT be shared?
questions.context: Pictures: a toothbrush, a book, a pen, a football.
questions.expected: A toothbrush
questions.memo: Toothbrushes touch your mouth and carry germs. Each person needs their own.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you share a face towel?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why shouldn't you share a face towel?
options: It can spread skin infections and germs
questions.expected: It can spread skin infections and germs
questions.memo: Face towels carry germs from your skin. Sharing them can spread infections like pink-eye.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a personal item — it IS okay to share?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is okay to share?
questions.expected: A book
questions.memo: Books, sports equipment, toys are fine to share. Items that touch your skin, mouth, eyes or private parts should stay personal.

questions.question: Where do germs LOVE to grow in a house?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where do germs love to grow in a house?
options: In warm, damp places like dirty kitchens and bathrooms
questions.expected: In warm, damp places like dirty kitchens and bathrooms
questions.memo: Germs need warmth, food and moisture to grow. Dirty dishes, food crumbs, damp bathrooms — all favourites.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for washing your hands well.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these steps in the right order for washing your hands.
options: Rub for 20 seconds, including thumbs and nails
Rinse and dry on a clean towel
questions.expected: Wet your hands,Use soap,Rub for 20 seconds, including thumbs and nails,Rinse and dry on a clean towel
questions.memo: Wet, soap, scrub all over for 20 seconds, rinse, dry. Hand-washing prevents many illnesses.

questions.question: When should you wash your hands?
questions.ruby_prompt: When are important times to wash your hands?
options: Before eating, after the toilet, and after coughing or sneezing
questions.expected: Before eating, after the toilet, and after coughing or sneezing
questions.memo: These three times stop most germs from getting into your body or onto others'.

questions.question: True or false: Brushing teeth twice a day keeps mouths healthy.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Brushing teeth twice a day helps keep your mouth healthy.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Twice a day — morning and night — is the standard. Don't forget the back teeth and along the gumline.

questions.question: Which is a 'germ-breeding area' in a kitchen?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a germ-breeding area in a kitchen?
questions.expected: A dirty dishcloth or sponge
questions.memo: Dishcloths and sponges hold food bits, water and germs. They should be rinsed, dried in the sun, and replaced often.

questions.question: Which bathroom item is a germ-breeding area if not cleaned?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which bathroom item becomes a germ-breeding area if it isn't cleaned?
questions.expected: The toilet seat and bowl
questions.memo: The toilet seat and bowl have lots of germs. Clean them often.

questions.question: Sipho coughs into his hand and then shakes a friend's hand. What's wrong?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho coughs into his hand and then shakes a friend's hand. What's wrong with that?
options: He's passed germs straight to his friend
questions.expected: He's passed germs straight to his friend
questions.memo: Cough/sneeze into your elbow or a tissue, not your hand. Then wash. That cuts the chain of germs.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep your nails short and clean?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are short clean nails important for hygiene?
options: Germs and dirt collect under long nails
Long nails make you sick by themselves
questions.expected: Germs and dirt collect under long nails
questions.memo: Dirt and germs hide under long nails. Keep them short and clean, especially before you eat.

questions.question: Which of these is a good daily hygiene habit?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a good daily hygiene habit?
options: Bathe or wash daily and wear clean clothes
questions.expected: Bathe or wash daily and wear clean clothes
questions.memo: Wash every day and wear clean clothes. It keeps your skin healthy and stops body smell.

questions.question: Sharing a toothbrush spreads:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sharing a toothbrush mostly spreads what?
options: Mouth germs and possible diseases like colds and gum infections
questions.expected: Mouth germs and possible diseases like colds and gum infections
questions.memo: Toothbrushes hold mouth germs — including those that cause colds, flu and even some serious infections. Always your own.

questions.question: Sun-drying laundry helps because:
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is sun-drying laundry good?
questions.expected: Sunlight kills many germs
questions.memo: Sunlight kills many germs, so drying washing in the sun helps keep it clean.

questions.question: True or false: It is okay to put your finger in your eye after touching dirty things.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It is okay to touch your eye with a finger that has touched dirty things.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Eyes are an easy way for germs to enter the body. Wash hands before touching your face or eyes.

questions.question: Karabo finds an old toothbrush on the floor. What should she do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo finds an old toothbrush lying on the floor. What should she do?
options: Throw it away — used toothbrushes are personal and used ones aren't safe
Put it in her own cup
questions.expected: Throw it away — used toothbrushes are personal and used ones aren't safe
questions.memo: Old toothbrushes carry germs and aren't yours. Bin them. Always start with a new clean brush of your own.

questions.question: Why is it important to flush the toilet and close the lid before flushing?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to flush the toilet AND close the lid before flushing?
options: Flushing without a lid can spray germs into the air
questions.expected: Flushing without a lid can spray germs into the air
questions.memo: When a toilet flushes, tiny droplets fly out. Closing the lid keeps those droplets from landing on your toothbrush etc.

questions.question: Which is a good rule for keeping food safe in the house?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a good rule for keeping food safe in the house?
options: Cover food and keep raw meat away from cooked food
Put raw chicken on top of fruit
questions.expected: Cover food and keep raw meat away from cooked food
questions.memo: Covering food keeps flies and germs out. Raw meat juices carry germs — keep them away from food that won't be cooked again.

questions.question: Tell me one personal item you should NOT share.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one personal item you should never share with someone else.
questions.expected: A toothbrush
questions.memo: Don't share your toothbrush. Combs, face towels and cups shouldn't be shared either.

questions.question: Which sequence shows how germs spread from a dirty hand to make you sick?
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in the right order to show how germs from a dirty hand can make you sick.
questions.expected: Hand touches a dirty thing,Hand touches food or face,Germs enter the body,Person gets sick
questions.memo: Dirty thing → hand → food/face → inside body → sickness. Washing breaks the chain at the hand stage.

LS.L4.PSW.T13.title: Dietary habits of children
LS.L4.PSW.T13.description: Impact of dietary habits on dental and oral hygiene.
LS.L4.PSW.T13.recovery_strategy: Focus on the link between everyday food choices and how teeth feel. Avoid shaming favourite foods — frame as 'how often' and 'what to do after'.

questions.question: Which of these is bad for your teeth if eaten very often?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is bad for your teeth if eaten very often?
questions.context: Pictures: a sweet, an apple, a drop of water, a carrot.
questions.expected: Sweets and sugary fizzy drinks
questions.memo: Sugar feeds the germs in your mouth that cause tooth decay. Sweets and fizzy drinks are the biggest culprits.

questions.question: How many times a day should you brush your teeth?
questions.ruby_prompt: How many times a day should you brush your teeth?
questions.expected: Twice a day
questions.memo: Morning and night. Brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste protects your teeth.

questions.question: Which is BEST for your teeth to drink?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is best for your teeth to drink?
questions.expected: Water
questions.memo: Water has no sugar and helps wash food bits away. The best drink for your teeth and the rest of your body.

questions.question: What causes a 'cavity' (a hole in a tooth)?
questions.ruby_prompt: What causes a cavity — a hole in a tooth?
options: Germs that eat sugar on the teeth and produce acid
questions.expected: Germs that eat sugar on the teeth and produce acid
questions.memo: Mouth germs use leftover sugar to make acid. The acid eats away at the tooth, causing a cavity. Brushing removes both.

questions.question: True or false: Eating fruit between meals is better for teeth than eating sweets.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Eating fruit between meals is better for your teeth than eating sweets.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Fruit has natural sugar but also fibre and water. Sweets are concentrated sugar that sticks to teeth.

questions.question: Which is a HEALTHY snack for between meals?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a healthy snack to have between meals?
questions.expected: An apple or a carrot
questions.memo: An apple or a carrot is a healthy snack. It gives your body real goodness.

questions.question: Which food contains LOTS of hidden sugar?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these has lots of hidden sugar?
questions.context: Pictures: a fizzy drink, a drop of water, an apple, a bowl of pap.
questions.expected: Sweetened cold drink (cola, fanta)
questions.memo: One can of fizzy drink can have 8–10 teaspoons of sugar. That's why dentists worry about them most.

questions.question: What does FLUORIDE in toothpaste do?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does fluoride — the medicine in toothpaste — do?
options: Makes the outer layer of teeth stronger
questions.expected: Makes the outer layer of teeth stronger
questions.memo: Fluoride strengthens tooth enamel — the hard outer layer. Look for it on toothpaste labels.

questions.question: Lerato eats sweets all day at school. Her teeth start to hurt. What does she need to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato eats sweets all day at school. Her teeth start to hurt. What does she need to do?
options: See a dentist and cut down on sweets, brush twice a day
questions.expected: See a dentist and cut down on sweets, brush twice a day
questions.memo: Pain often means decay. Visit the dentist; in the meantime cut sweets, brush properly, and drink water.

questions.question: Which is true about milk for teeth?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is true about milk and teeth?
options: Milk has calcium which helps teeth and bones grow strong
Milk has lots of bad sugar
questions.expected: Milk has calcium which helps teeth and bones grow strong
questions.memo: Calcium is the mineral your teeth and bones are made of. Milk and yoghurt are good sources.

questions.question: Put these in order for brushing your teeth properly.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these steps in order for brushing your teeth properly.
options: Put a pea-size of toothpaste on the brush
Brush all sides of every tooth for 2 minutes
Rinse the brush and put it away to dry
questions.expected: Put a pea-size of toothpaste on the brush,Brush all sides of every tooth for 2 minutes,Spit out the toothpaste,Rinse the brush and put it away to dry
questions.memo: Put a pea-sized bit of toothpaste on the brush. Brush every side of every tooth for 2 minutes. Spit. Rinse the brush.

questions.question: True or false: If you eat well, you never need to see a dentist.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: If you eat healthy food, you never need to see a dentist.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Even healthy eaters need check-ups — once or twice a year. A dentist spots small problems before they become big ones.

questions.question: Sipho's mouth feels sticky after sweets. Why?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's mouth feels sticky after sweets. Why?
options: Sugar coats his teeth and feeds the germs
questions.expected: Sugar coats his teeth and feeds the germs
questions.memo: His mouth feels sticky because sugar is coating his teeth. The sugar feeds germs.

questions.question: After eating, what's a quick thing you can do for your teeth if you can't brush?
questions.ruby_prompt: After eating, what's a quick thing you can do for your teeth if you can't brush right away?
questions.expected: Rinse your mouth with water
questions.memo: Water rinses sugar and food bits off your teeth. Best second-best when a brush isn't there.

questions.question: Which is BEST as a lunch-pack drink for school?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is the best drink to pack for school?
questions.expected: Water
questions.memo: Water for thirst, every day. Save sweet drinks for special occasions, not for school lunches.

questions.question: Sticky sweets are worse than chocolate that melts away because:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sticky sweets are worse for teeth than chocolate that melts away. Why?
options: Sticky sweets cling to teeth for longer, giving germs more time to make acid
questions.expected: Sticky sweets cling to teeth for longer, giving germs more time to make acid
questions.memo: Sticky sweets stay on your teeth longer, so germs have more time to make acid that hurts teeth.

questions.question: Tell me one healthy snack you like.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one healthy snack that you like.
questions.expected: An apple
questions.memo: Fruit, like an apple or a banana, is a healthy snack. So are carrots and plain yoghurt.

questions.question: Which group of food helps keep your gums healthy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which food group helps keep your gums healthy?
questions.expected: Fruits and vegetables (vitamin C)
questions.memo: Vitamin C in fruit and veg keeps gums strong. Without it, gums can bleed and teeth can loosen.

questions.question: Why is going to bed without brushing especially bad?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is going to sleep without brushing your teeth especially bad?
options: Germs work on sugar all night while you sleep
questions.expected: Germs work on sugar all night while you sleep
questions.memo: While you sleep, less saliva flows. Germs have a long quiet party with any sugar left on your teeth. Always brush before bed.

questions.question: Mpho eats sweets daily AND never brushes. What is most likely to happen?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho eats sweets every day AND never brushes her teeth. What is most likely to happen?
options: Cavities, tooth pain and possibly losing teeth
questions.expected: Cavities, tooth pain and possibly losing teeth
questions.memo: Sweets every day and no brushing cause holes, tooth pain, and maybe losing teeth.

LS.L4.PSW.T14.title: Healthy environment and personal health
LS.L4.PSW.T14.description: Home, school and community. Unhealthy environments (air, water, land pollution, illegal dumping), dangers to personal health, conservation strategies, Arbor Day.
LS.L4.PSW.T14.recovery_strategy: Connect the environment to the learner's daily life and health — air at home, water from the tap, litter outside the gate. Small actions matter.

questions.question: What is 'pollution'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does the word 'pollution' mean?
options: Dirt or harmful things in the air, water or land
questions.expected: Dirt or harmful things in the air, water or land
questions.memo: Pollution is dirt or harmful things in the air, the water or the land, like smoke and plastic.

questions.question: Which is an example of LAND pollution?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is an example of land pollution?
options: Plastic bottles and rubbish thrown on the ground
questions.expected: Plastic bottles and rubbish thrown on the ground
questions.memo: Land pollution = rubbish on the ground. Plastics last hundreds of years and harm animals that eat or get tangled in them.

questions.question: Which is an example of WATER pollution?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is an example of water pollution?
options: Factory chemicals or sewage in a river
Children playing in a clean pool
questions.expected: Factory chemicals or sewage in a river
questions.memo: Factory chemicals or sewage in a river is water pollution. It kills fish and makes people sick.

questions.question: Which is an example of AIR pollution?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is an example of air pollution?
options: Smoke from factories, fires and many cars
questions.expected: Smoke from factories, fires and many cars
questions.memo: Smoke and exhaust fumes pollute air. Long-term, polluted air causes lung diseases and worsens asthma.

questions.question: What is an 'illegal dumping site'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is an illegal dumping site?
options: A place where people dump rubbish where they shouldn't
questions.expected: A place where people dump rubbish where they shouldn't
questions.memo: Illegal dumping is leaving rubbish in places it shouldn't go, like empty land or riverbanks. It is against the law.

questions.question: Why is illegal dumping bad for health?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is illegal dumping bad for our health?
options: Rotting rubbish attracts rats, flies and disease
It makes the area look nicer
questions.expected: Rotting rubbish attracts rats, flies and disease
questions.memo: Dumped rubbish breeds rats, flies and mosquitoes, which spread disease. It also pollutes water and soil.

questions.question: True or false: One person picking up litter doesn't matter.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: One person picking up litter doesn't really matter.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Every piece of litter you pick up helps. And one person often gets others to help too.

questions.question: Which is a way to keep your home environment HEALTHY?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a way to keep your home environment healthy?
options: Empty bins, sweep, and let fresh air in
questions.expected: Empty bins, sweep, and let fresh air in
questions.memo: Clean surfaces, regular bin emptying, and ventilation keep a home healthy. Trapped damp and dust cause illness.

questions.question: What does 'conservation' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does 'conservation' mean?
options: Looking after and protecting nature for the future
questions.expected: Looking after and protecting nature for the future
questions.memo: Conservation = caring for water, trees, soil and wildlife so they last. It's how the planet stays able to look after us.

questions.question: Arbor Day is a day for:
questions.ruby_prompt: Arbor Day is a day for what?
questions.expected: Planting and caring for trees
questions.memo: Arbor Day (in early September in SA) is when schools and communities plant trees. Trees clean air and give shade.

questions.question: Which is a way to use LESS water at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to use less water at home?
options: Take shorter showers and fix leaks
Wash one dish in lots of water
questions.expected: Take shorter showers and fix leaks
questions.memo: Take shorter showers and fix leaking taps. That saves a lot of water.

questions.question: Why are trees important for our environment?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are trees so important for our environment?
options: They clean the air, give shade, and prevent soil from washing away
questions.expected: They clean the air, give shade, and prevent soil from washing away
questions.memo: Trees clean air, hold soil, give shade, cool cities, and make oxygen. One mature tree does a lot of work.

questions.question: Which is a kind of recycling?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is recycling?
options: Putting plastic bottles and paper in special bins to be reused
questions.expected: Putting plastic bottles and paper in special bins to be reused
questions.memo: Recycling = turning used things into new things. Many SA towns have recycling pickers — sorting helps them.

questions.question: Put these in order for what to do with an empty plastic bottle.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what you should do with an empty plastic bottle.
options: Crush it to take less space
Put it in a recycling bin or hand it to a recycler
questions.expected: Empty out any liquid,Crush it to take less space,Put it in a recycling bin or hand it to a recycler,Don't litter or burn it
questions.memo: Empty the bottle. Crush it. Put it in a recycling bin. Never litter it or burn it.

questions.question: True or false: Burning plastic at home is a good way to get rid of it.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Burning plastic at home is a good way to get rid of it.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Burning plastic releases poisonous smoke that harms your lungs. Recycle or take to a proper waste site.

questions.question: Sipho lives near an illegal dumping site. His chest is often sore. The link is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho lives near an illegal dumping site. His chest is often sore. What's the link?
options: Burning rubbish and dust can hurt his lungs
questions.expected: Burning rubbish and dust can hurt his lungs
questions.memo: Dust and smoke from dumps trigger coughs, asthma and chest problems. Cleaning up dumps is a health issue, not just looks.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you can do to look after the environment.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one thing you can do to look after the environment.
questions.expected: Pick up litter when I see it
questions.memo: You can pick up litter, plant a tree, save water or recycle.

questions.question: When is South African Arbor Day usually celebrated?
questions.ruby_prompt: When is South African Arbor Day (or Arbor Week) usually celebrated?
questions.expected: Early September each year
questions.memo: Arbor Week is in early September in SA — the start of spring, the right time to plant.

questions.question: A community clean-up day helps because:
questions.ruby_prompt: Why does a community clean-up day help?
options: Many hands remove a lot of litter and people care more afterwards
questions.expected: Many hands remove a lot of litter and people care more afterwards
questions.memo: Many people can pick up lots of litter fast. Afterwards, people care more about keeping the place clean.

questions.question: Which is the BEST description of a healthy environment?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is the best description of a healthy environment?
options: Clean air, clean water, trees and green spaces, no rubbish
questions.expected: Clean air, clean water, trees and green spaces, no rubbish
questions.memo: Healthy = clean air, clean water, places for plants and wildlife, and waste handled properly. It supports our health too.

LS.L4.PSW.T15.title: HIV and AIDS: basic facts
LS.L4.PSW.T15.description: Basic explanation of HIV and AIDS, transmission through blood, how HIV is not transmitted, protecting oneself against infection through blood.
LS.L4.PSW.T15.recovery_strategy: Be factual and calm. HIV is treatable. Reinforce: people with HIV are not 'bad' or 'dangerous'; you cannot catch HIV from everyday contact like hugging, sharing food or sitting next to someone.

questions.question: What does HIV stand for in short?
questions.ruby_prompt: HIV is a name for a virus. What does HIV stand for, very simply?
options: Human Immunodeficiency Virus — it weakens the body's protection
questions.expected: Human Immunodeficiency Virus — it weakens the body's protection
questions.memo: HIV is a virus. It attacks the body's immune system — the part that fights off germs. People can live with HIV with proper medicine.

questions.question: What does AIDS stand for in short?
questions.ruby_prompt: AIDS is a condition that can happen if HIV is not treated. What does AIDS mean simply?
options: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome — when the body can no longer fight off many illnesses
questions.expected: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome — when the body can no longer fight off many illnesses
questions.memo: AIDS happens later, only if HIV is not treated. With good medicine, people with HIV may never get AIDS.

questions.question: Can you catch HIV from hugging someone with HIV?
questions.ruby_prompt: Can you catch HIV from hugging someone who has HIV?
options: No — HIV is not spread by everyday contact like hugging
questions.expected: No — HIV is not spread by everyday contact like hugging
questions.memo: No. You can't get HIV from hugs, handshakes or sharing a meal.

questions.question: Can you catch HIV from sharing food or a cup with someone who has HIV?
questions.ruby_prompt: Can you catch HIV from sharing food or a cup with someone who has HIV?
options: Only if you eat all the food
questions.expected: No
questions.memo: Sharing food, drinks, plates, cups — none of these spread HIV. Children with HIV are safe to be with at school.

questions.question: True or false: A person with HIV can take medicine and live a long healthy life.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: A person with HIV can take medicine and live a long healthy life.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. HIV medicine (called ARVs) is free in SA. People who take it daily can live full long lives.

questions.question: One way HIV CAN spread through blood is:
questions.ruby_prompt: One way HIV can spread between people is through blood. Which is an example?
options: Using a needle that already had someone else's blood on it
questions.expected: Using a needle that already had someone else's blood on it
questions.memo: HIV spreads through certain body fluids, especially blood. Used needles are one way — never touch a needle you find.

questions.question: If you see a used needle on the ground, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you see a used needle lying on the ground, what should you do?
options: Tell a grown-up — never pick it up yourself
Pick it up to look at it
questions.expected: Tell a grown-up — never pick it up yourself
questions.memo: Needles can have blood on them and carry HIV or other diseases. Tell an adult — they will dispose of it safely.

questions.question: If a friend is bleeding and needs help, what should you do safely?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend is bleeding. They need help. How can you help safely?
options: Tell a grown-up and use a clean cloth, gloves if you have them
Touch the blood with your bare hands
questions.expected: Tell a grown-up and use a clean cloth, gloves if you have them
questions.memo: Get an adult. If you must help quickly, use a cloth between your hand and the wound — gloves are even better. Always wash your hands afterwards.

questions.question: True or false: You can tell if someone has HIV by looking at them.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: You can tell if someone has HIV just by looking at them.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: You cannot tell. People with HIV look like everyone else. The only way to know is a blood test.

questions.question: Where can a person be tested for HIV in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where in South Africa can a person be tested for HIV?
options: At any government clinic — testing is free and private
Only at one hospital in the whole country
Only by paying lots of money
questions.expected: At any government clinic — testing is free and private
questions.memo: Free, private HIV tests are at all government clinics. Many also offer ARVs free if needed.

questions.question: A child at school has HIV. The right thing for classmates to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: A child at school has HIV. What's the right thing for classmates to do?
options: Treat them like any other friend — they cannot infect you in normal play
questions.expected: Treat them like any other friend — they cannot infect you in normal play
questions.memo: Children with HIV go to school like everyone else. HIV doesn't spread through everyday play. Kindness matters most.

questions.question: Why is it important NOT to make fun of people with HIV?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important not to make fun of someone with HIV?
options: People with HIV are sick because of a virus, not because they did anything wrong — they need our care
Because it's illegal to be kind
questions.expected: People with HIV are sick because of a virus, not because they did anything wrong — they need our care
questions.memo: HIV is a virus, not a punishment. Making fun adds pain and stops people from getting tested and treated. Stigma kills.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way HIV spreads?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is NOT a way that HIV spreads?
options: Used needles with blood on them
Mother to baby during birth without medicine
questions.expected: Mosquito bites
questions.memo: Mosquitoes don't spread HIV. HIV spreads through certain body fluids, like blood.

questions.question: What are 'ARVs' (the medicine for HIV)?
questions.ruby_prompt: What are ARVs — the medicine for HIV?
options: Pills that stop HIV from making people sick
questions.expected: Pills that stop HIV from making people sick
questions.memo: ARVs are pills taken every day that stop HIV from making people sick. In South Africa they are free.

questions.question: Put these in order for what to do if you see blood on a cut or grazes.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what to do if you see blood from a cut.
options: Use a cloth or gloves to press on the cut
questions.expected: Don't touch the blood directly,Call or fetch a grown-up,Use a cloth or gloves to press on the cut,Wash your hands well afterwards
questions.memo: Don't touch, get an adult, protect your hands while helping, wash. This is good hygiene AND prevents HIV through blood.

questions.question: True or false: Sharing a toothbrush with someone with HIV is safe.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Sharing a toothbrush with someone with HIV is safe.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Toothbrushes can have tiny amounts of blood from gums on them. Sharing them is one of the few in-the-home risks. Each person their own — always.

questions.question: Lerato hears a rumour that you can get HIV from a swimming pool. What's true?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato hears a rumour that you can get HIV from a swimming pool. What's the truth?
options: You cannot — HIV does not spread through water, pools, taps or showers
questions.expected: You cannot — HIV does not spread through water, pools, taps or showers
questions.memo: HIV doesn't survive in water. Pools, taps, baths — all safe. Many myths about HIV exist; the clinic and your teacher have the facts.

questions.question: Tell me one way HIV does NOT spread.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one way that HIV does NOT spread.
questions.expected: Hugging or shaking hands
questions.memo: HIV does not spread through hugging, shaking hands, or sharing food and cups.

questions.question: If a classmate has HIV and a learner says something unkind, the right thing to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: If a classmate has HIV and someone says something unkind about them, what's the right thing to do?
options: Tell them HIV doesn't spread by everyday contact and report it to a teacher
questions.expected: Tell them HIV doesn't spread by everyday contact and report it to a teacher
questions.memo: Tell them HIV doesn't spread by touching or playing together, and tell a teacher. People with HIV need friends.

questions.question: Which sentence is TRUE about HIV today?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these statements is true about HIV today?
options: HIV can be treated. People with HIV who take ARVs daily can live full long lives.
HIV is always fatal in a year.
HIV is contagious in the air.
questions.expected: HIV can be treated. People with HIV who take ARVs daily can live full long lives.
questions.memo: HIV can be treated. People who take ARVs every day can live long, full lives.

LS.L5.PSW.T01.title: Positive self-concept formation
LS.L5.PSW.T01.description: Influence of adults and peers on self-concept, personal successes as contributors to a positive self-concept, action plan for continued positive self-concept formation.
LS.L5.PSW.T01.recovery_strategy: Affirm that self-concept grows from many small wins and from kind voices around us. Help the learner identify supportive people and one strength they can build on.

questions.question: What is 'self-concept'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Let's start with the words. What does 'self-concept' mean?
options: The way you see and think about yourself
The time you go to bed
questions.expected: The way you see and think about yourself
questions.memo: Self-concept is your inner picture of yourself — your strengths, your worth, what you can do. It grows over time.

questions.question: A POSITIVE self-concept means you mostly think:
questions.ruby_prompt: Someone with a positive self-concept mostly thinks what about themselves?
options: 'I am valuable and I can learn and grow.'
'I am useless and can't do anything.'
questions.expected: 'I am valuable and I can learn and grow.'
questions.memo: A positive self-concept means believing 'I matter, and I can learn and grow'. It isn't bragging or putting yourself down.

questions.question: Which adults can SHAPE a child's self-concept?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which adults shape how a child sees themselves?
options: Parents, teachers, family members and caregivers
questions.expected: Parents, teachers, family members and caregivers
questions.memo: The grown-ups closest to you, like parents, teachers and family, shape how you see yourself.

questions.question: True or false: Friends and peers can also affect how you see yourself.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Friends and peers also affect how you see yourself.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — friends shape our self-concept too. Kind friends help us grow; unkind ones can hurt our self-image. Choose friends carefully.

questions.question: Thandi did well at her school athletics. How does this affect her self-concept?
questions.ruby_prompt: Thandi did really well at school athletics. How does this affect her self-concept?
options: It builds her positive self-concept — she sees herself as capable
questions.expected: It builds her positive self-concept — she sees herself as capable
questions.memo: Real successes — small or big — are the building blocks of a healthy self-concept. They give us proof we can do things.

questions.question: Which of these is a 'personal success' that builds self-concept?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a personal success that builds your self-concept?
options: Finishing a hard piece of homework on my own
questions.expected: Finishing a hard piece of homework on my own
questions.memo: Personal successes are things YOU did with effort — they grow your sense that you can. Watching TV doesn't change your self-view.

questions.question: When an adult says, 'I'm proud of you for trying,' it usually:
questions.ruby_prompt: When an adult says 'I'm proud of you for trying,' what does that usually do for a child?
options: Helps the child see themselves as someone who can keep trying
questions.expected: Helps the child see themselves as someone who can keep trying
questions.memo: Praise for EFFORT (not just results) builds a strong self-concept. It tells the child: trying is what matters, and I am someone who tries.

questions.question: Sipho's friends keep telling him he is bad at maths. How might this affect him?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's friends keep telling him he is bad at maths. How might this affect him over time?
options: He may start to believe it and stop trying — even though it's not the truth
He will get better at maths instantly
questions.expected: He may start to believe it and stop trying — even though it's not the truth
questions.memo: What people repeat to us, we often start to believe. This is why unkind friends hurt self-concept. Sipho needs voices that tell him the truth: he CAN learn maths.

questions.question: What's an 'action plan' for self-concept?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's an 'action plan' for building your self-concept?
options: A simple list of small steps to grow your strengths and confidence
questions.expected: A simple list of small steps to grow your strengths and confidence
questions.memo: An action plan is real and small: practise reading 10 minutes a day; ask one new person to play this week. Self-concept grows through action, not wishing.

questions.question: Put these in order for making a small action plan to build your self-concept.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order — making a small action plan to build your self-concept.
options: Notice one strength or area you want to grow
Choose one small step you can take this week
Do the step and notice how you feel afterwards
questions.expected: Notice one strength or area you want to grow,Choose one small step you can take this week,Do the step and notice how you feel afterwards,Plan the next step
questions.memo: Notice → step → reflect → next step. Self-concept builds through tiny repeated wins, not one big leap.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you did well recently.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one thing you did well recently that you feel good about.
questions.expected: I helped my younger brother with his homework
questions.memo: Good answers: any real success — finished a task, learned a new skill, helped someone, controlled my temper, told the truth. All of these build self-concept.

questions.question: True or false: Self-concept can grow over time.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Self-concept can grow stronger over time.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — self-concept is not fixed. With supportive people and real successes, it grows. With unkind voices, it can shrink — but that can be turned around.

questions.question: Karabo failed a test. The healthiest response is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo failed a test. What's the healthiest response for her self-concept?
options: 'I didn't do well this time. I will study more for next time.'
questions.expected: 'I didn't do well this time. I will study more for next time.'
questions.memo: A healthy self-concept survives failure — because failing one test isn't the same as being a failure. Learners with strong self-concept bounce back.

questions.question: Which is a way ADULTS can damage a child's self-concept?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these damages a child's self-concept?
options: Calling them names or comparing them harshly to others
questions.expected: Calling them names or comparing them harshly to others
questions.memo: Name-calling and comparison teach children to see themselves as 'less than'. Adults' words leave deep marks — good and bad.

questions.question: Which sentence shows a positive self-concept?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which sentence shows a positive self-concept?
options: 'I am learning and growing every day.'
questions.expected: 'I am learning and growing every day.'
questions.memo: 'I am learning and growing every day' shows you believe in yourself without bragging.

questions.question: Mpho can't draw well yet, but she wants to. What action plan would help?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho wants to get better at drawing. What action plan would help build her self-concept around art?
options: Draw a small picture each day for two weeks and notice progress
Compare every drawing to a master artist
questions.expected: Draw a small picture each day for two weeks and notice progress
questions.memo: Drawing a little every day and noticing how she improves will help Mpho. Comparing herself to experts won't.

questions.question: Why is comparing yourself to others harmful?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why does comparing yourself to other people often hurt your self-concept?
options: Each person has different gifts and different starting points
questions.expected: Each person has different gifts and different starting points
questions.memo: Everyone has different gifts and starts in a different place. Compare yourself with how you were before.

questions.question: Which of these helps a child build a strong self-concept at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these helps a child build self-concept at home?
options: Adults who listen, praise effort, and let them try things
Being told they can't do things
questions.expected: Adults who listen, praise effort, and let them try things
questions.memo: A child who is heard and supported grows confident. Letting them try (and sometimes fail) is part of that.

questions.question: True or false: A child can build self-concept even if some adults around them are harsh.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: A child can still build a positive self-concept even if some adults around them are harsh.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — even one kind adult, one supportive teacher, one good friend can help a child build self-concept. Hold onto the supportive voices.

questions.question: Which is the BEST starting place to grow your self-concept?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the best starting place to grow your self-concept?
options: Notice one thing you already do well, and build on it with practice
Wait for someone to save you
questions.expected: Notice one thing you already do well, and build on it with practice
questions.memo: Self-concept grows from REAL strengths. Find one. Practise it. Notice progress. Pick the next one. That's the recipe.

LS.L5.PSW.T02.title: Giving and receiving feedback
LS.L5.PSW.T02.description: Appropriate ways of giving positive and negative feedback to peers; appropriate ways of receiving feedback from peers and adults.
LS.L5.PSW.T02.recovery_strategy: Feedback is a gift, even when it stings. Help the learner separate the message from the messenger and practise calm responses.

questions.question: What is 'feedback'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is feedback?
options: Information someone gives you about how you did something
questions.expected: Information someone gives you about how you did something
questions.memo: Feedback tells you what went well or what could be better. It helps you grow.

questions.question: Which is an example of POSITIVE feedback?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is an example of positive feedback?
options: 'I really like how you helped Lebo today.'
questions.expected: 'I really like how you helped Lebo today.'
questions.memo: 'I really like how you helped Lebo today' is positive feedback. It names the good thing.

questions.question: Which is an example of HELPFUL negative feedback?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is an example of helpful negative feedback — feedback that points out something to fix, but in a kind way?
options: 'Your handwriting is hard to read here — try writing a bit bigger next time.'
questions.expected: 'Your handwriting is hard to read here — try writing a bit bigger next time.'
questions.memo: Helpful negative feedback points out the issue AND offers a way forward. Insults are not feedback.

questions.question: When giving feedback, you should focus on:
questions.ruby_prompt: When giving feedback, what should you focus on?
options: The work or action — not the whole person
Other people they should be like
questions.expected: The work or action — not the whole person
questions.memo: Feedback is about what someone DID, not who they ARE. 'Your essay needs more detail' — not 'you are bad at writing'.

questions.question: True or false: Telling someone exactly what they did wrong is the same as being mean.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Telling someone what they did wrong is the same as being mean.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: They are not the same. Kind, specific feedback HELPS people. Insults hurt. The difference is in how it's said and why.

questions.question: Which is the BEST way to give feedback to a friend?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the best way to give feedback to a friend?
options: In private, kindly, and naming both what worked and what to improve
In front of everyone to shame them
questions.expected: In private, kindly, and naming both what worked and what to improve
questions.memo: Give feedback in private, kindly. Say what worked and what could be better.

questions.question: Your teacher tells you your essay needs more detail. The best response is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Your teacher says your essay needs more detail. What's the best response?
options: Say thanks, ask 'where exactly?', and try again
Tell the teacher she is wrong
Cry and refuse to write again
questions.expected: Say thanks, ask 'where exactly?', and try again
questions.memo: Receiving feedback well = listen, accept, ask questions, act on it. That is how learners grow.

questions.question: Sipho's classmate says, 'Your project is great but the picture is upside down.' Sipho should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's classmate says, 'Your project is great but the picture is upside down.' What's the best response?
options: 'Thanks for noticing! Let me fix it.'
questions.expected: 'Thanks for noticing! Let me fix it.'
questions.memo: A small fix saves him from a bigger embarrassment. The classmate was actually being helpful — Sipho's friend, not enemy.

questions.question: True or false: You can disagree with feedback after thinking about it.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: You can disagree with feedback after thinking about it.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — not all feedback is right. After listening calmly, you can decide what to act on. But hear it first.

questions.question: What's a calm response when feedback hurts a little?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a calm response when feedback hurts a little?
options: Breathe, thank them, and think about it later
Burst into tears in front of everyone
questions.expected: Breathe, thank them, and think about it later
questions.memo: Hard feedback stings — that's normal. Buying time with a calm 'thanks, let me think' protects the relationship AND you.

questions.question: Put these in order for giving feedback to a classmate.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for giving good feedback to a classmate.
options: Find a kind way to say what could improve
Say both — what's good first, then the improvement
questions.expected: Notice what works well,Find a kind way to say what could improve,Say both — what's good first, then the improvement,Ask if they have questions
questions.memo: Notice, soften the improvement, share both, check in. This 'sandwich' of feedback is widely used because it lands well.

questions.question: Which is NOT feedback — it's just rude?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is not feedback — it's just rude?
options: 'Your maths working is missing a step here.'
'I think your story would be even better with one more example.'
questions.expected: 'You're horrible.'
questions.memo: 'You're horrible' attacks the person and doesn't help. It is an insult, not feedback.

questions.question: Tell me one POSITIVE feedback you could give to a classmate.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me a positive piece of feedback you could give to a classmate today.
questions.expected: I liked how you helped me with my maths today
questions.memo: Good answers: any specific, kind, true compliment about something they DID. Specific is much better than 'you're nice'.

questions.question: Why is it important to RECEIVE feedback well, even when it's negative?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to receive feedback well, even when it's negative?
options: Feedback is one of the fastest ways to learn and grow
questions.expected: Feedback is one of the fastest ways to learn and grow
questions.memo: People who can hear feedback grow faster than people who can't. It's a real life skill.

questions.question: Lerato just performed a song. Mpho says, 'I loved the start. The middle was a bit fast — try slower.' This is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato just performed a song. Mpho says, 'I loved the start. The middle was a bit fast — try slower.' What kind of feedback is this?
options: Balanced and helpful — both positive and improvement, specific
questions.expected: Balanced and helpful — both positive and improvement, specific
questions.memo: Mpho said what was good and what to fix, clearly. That is balanced, helpful feedback.

questions.question: When a friend gives you feedback you don't like, the WORST thing to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: When a friend gives you feedback you don't like, what's the worst thing to do?
options: Attack them or stop being their friend
questions.expected: Attack them or stop being their friend
questions.memo: If you attack your friend for honest feedback, you might lose the friendship, and people stop telling you the truth.

questions.question: Karabo gets feedback from her teacher, her mother and her friend. Should they all agree?
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo gets feedback from her teacher, her mom and her friend. Will they all agree?
options: Maybe not — different people notice different things
Only one of them is right
questions.expected: Maybe not — different people notice different things
questions.memo: Different people see different sides. The pattern across many people's feedback is what matters more than any one piece.

questions.question: True or false: Saying 'thank you' is a good way to end receiving feedback, even if you disagree.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Saying 'thank you' is a good way to end receiving feedback, even if you disagree.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — thanks acknowledges the effort the other person made. You can still decide later what to do with the feedback.

questions.question: Which feedback is SPECIFIC enough to act on?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which feedback is specific enough that the person could actually act on it?
options: 'Your second paragraph needs an example to support the point.'
questions.expected: 'Your second paragraph needs an example to support the point.'
questions.memo: Specific feedback points to the exact place AND the exact fix. Vague feedback ('bad', 'try harder') doesn't help.

questions.question: Why might an adult sometimes give feedback that feels hard?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why might an adult give feedback that feels hard to hear?
options: Because they want you to grow and they see what you can become
questions.expected: Because they want you to grow and they see what you can become
questions.memo: Loving adults often see our potential more clearly than we do. Their hard feedback usually comes from belief in us, not from cruelty.

LS.L5.PSW.T03.title: Coping with emotions
LS.L5.PSW.T03.description: Empathy, compassion, anger, disappointment and sadness. Skills to manage emotions positively; the significance of friends in times of sadness, tragedy and change.
LS.L5.PSW.T03.recovery_strategy: Normalise all emotions; focus on healthy ways to express them. If a learner shares a tough feeling, validate first, then offer practical coping ideas.

questions.question: What is 'empathy'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does the word 'empathy' mean?
options: Understanding and sharing how someone else feels
questions.expected: Understanding and sharing how someone else feels
questions.memo: Empathy is feeling alongside someone — putting yourself in their shoes. It's a key skill for friendship.

questions.question: What is 'compassion'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is compassion?
options: Caring about someone's pain and wanting to help
questions.expected: Caring about someone's pain and wanting to help
questions.memo: Compassion means caring about someone's pain and wanting to help them.

questions.question: Sipho's grandmother passed away. He feels deep sadness. This feeling is called:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's grandmother passed away. The deep sadness he feels has a name. What is it?
questions.context: Pictures: a crying face, a hungry face, a bored face, a celebrating face.
questions.expected: Grief
questions.memo: Grief is the deep sadness of losing someone we love. It comes in waves and is normal.

questions.question: What is 'disappointment'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is disappointment?
options: The feeling when something doesn't go the way you hoped
questions.expected: The feeling when something doesn't go the way you hoped
questions.memo: Disappointment comes when our hopes meet a different reality. It's normal and can teach us to hope wisely.

questions.question: Which is a HEALTHY way to manage anger?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a healthy way to manage anger?
options: Walk away, breathe slowly, then talk about it
questions.expected: Walk away, breathe slowly, then talk about it
questions.memo: Walk away, breathe slowly to calm down, then talk about it.

questions.question: True or false: All feelings are okay to have, even unpleasant ones.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: All feelings are okay to have, even the hard ones.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — feelings aren't right or wrong. What matters is what we DO with them. Anger is okay; hitting isn't.

questions.question: Lerato's friend's parent died. The most important thing Lerato can do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato's friend's parent has died. What's the most important thing Lerato can do?
options: Be there — listen, hug, sit quietly. She doesn't need to 'fix' it
Tell her friend to stop crying
Tell jokes to cheer her up
questions.expected: Be there — listen, hug, sit quietly. She doesn't need to 'fix' it
questions.memo: Grieving people don't need fixing or cheering — they need someone to BE with them. Presence beats words.

questions.question: Why are friends so important during sad times?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are friends so important when something sad happens?
options: They remind us we are not alone and care about us
questions.expected: They remind us we are not alone and care about us
questions.memo: Sadness feels lighter when shared. A friend who listens — even without saying anything — gives huge comfort.

questions.question: Which is a way to manage SADNESS in a healthy way?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a healthy way to manage sadness?
options: Talk to someone you trust and let yourself cry if you need to
questions.expected: Talk to someone you trust and let yourself cry if you need to
questions.memo: Sadness needs to be felt and shared, not buried. Talking to a trusted person and letting tears come is healthy.

questions.question: Mpho is angry because her brother broke her toy. The healthy first step is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho is angry because her brother broke her toy. What's the healthy first step?
options: Take a few deep breaths before saying anything
questions.expected: Take a few deep breaths before saying anything
questions.memo: Breath before action calms the body. Once calm, words are much more powerful than fists or tears.

questions.question: When a friend is grieving, you should NOT say:
questions.ruby_prompt: When a friend is grieving, which of these is NOT a kind thing to say?
options: 'I am so sorry. I'm here for you.'
questions.expected: 'Just get over it.'
questions.memo: 'Get over it' rushes grief. Grief takes time. The other three sentences all show real support.

questions.question: Karabo doesn't make the school netball team. She feels disappointed. A healthy response is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo doesn't make the school netball team. She is disappointed. What's a healthy response?
options: Let herself feel sad, then plan more practice for next time
Tell everyone she didn't want to be in it anyway
questions.expected: Let herself feel sad, then plan more practice for next time
questions.memo: Disappointment hurts. Feeling it briefly, then deciding on the next move is the path of growth.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for calming down a strong feeling.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for calming down when a strong feeling hits.
options: Notice the feeling and name it (anger, fear, sadness)
Move your body — walk, breathe, drink water
Talk to a friend or trusted adult
Decide what to do once you're calm
questions.expected: Notice the feeling and name it (anger, fear, sadness),Move your body — walk, breathe, drink water,Talk to a friend or trusted adult,Decide what to do once you're calm
questions.memo: Name → move → connect → decide. Name-it-to-tame-it is real — naming a feeling shrinks its power.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you do that helps you feel calmer when you're upset.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one thing you do that helps you feel calmer when you're upset.
questions.expected: I take deep breaths and count to ten
questions.memo: Good answers: deep breaths, walk outside, drink water, talk to mom/dad, draw, listen to music, hug a pet, run. Find yours and use it.

questions.question: Which shows EMPATHY?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these shows empathy?
options: 'I can see this is really hard for you.'
questions.expected: 'I can see this is really hard for you.'
questions.memo: Empathy names the other person's feelings out loud. It says 'I see you' more than 'I have a fix'.

questions.question: True or false: A big change (like moving home) can bring many feelings at once.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: A big change like moving home can bring many feelings at once.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — big changes bring excitement, fear, sadness, hope, all mixed. All those feelings are normal.

questions.question: Sipho feels his anger building. What's a quick on-the-spot tool?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho can feel his anger building up. What's a quick tool he can use on the spot?
options: Slow deep breaths — in for 4, out for 6
Yell as loud as he can
questions.expected: Slow deep breaths — in for 4, out for 6
questions.memo: Slow breathing calms the nervous system fast. Longer out-breath than in-breath is the trick. Works in seconds.

questions.question: When a feeling is too big to handle alone, the BEST step is:
questions.ruby_prompt: When a feeling is too big to handle alone, what's the best step?
options: Tell a trusted adult — a parent, teacher, counsellor — or call Childline 116
questions.expected: Tell a trusted adult — a parent, teacher, counsellor — or call Childline 116
questions.memo: Asking for help is brave, not weak. Childline 116 is free in SA and listens to any worry.

questions.question: Which is a sign your friend might need support?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these might be a sign your friend needs your support?
options: They become very quiet, don't play, look tired and sad
questions.expected: They become very quiet, don't play, look tired and sad
questions.memo: Big changes in behaviour can mean someone is struggling inside. Notice the change and gently check in.

questions.question: What's the difference between empathy and sympathy?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the difference between empathy and sympathy?
options: Empathy = feeling WITH someone. Sympathy = feeling sorry FOR them.
questions.expected: Empathy = feeling WITH someone. Sympathy = feeling sorry FOR them.
questions.memo: Empathy is feeling with someone: 'I understand, I've felt that too.' Sympathy is feeling sorry for them.

LS.L5.PSW.T04.title: Relationships with peers, older people and strangers
LS.L5.PSW.T04.description: Safe and unsafe relationships, bad and good relationships, benefits of good and safe relationships.
LS.L5.PSW.T04.recovery_strategy: Affirm the learner's instincts — if something feels wrong, it usually is. Reinforce trusted-adult paths. Be calm and matter-of-fact about stranger safety.

questions.question: What is a 'peer'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a peer?
options: Someone about the same age as you
questions.expected: Someone about the same age as you
questions.memo: Peers are people roughly your age. Classmates, friends in your grade, kids at your sports club — all peers.

questions.question: Which is a GOOD relationship?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a good relationship?
options: One where both people respect, listen and care about each other
One where one person bosses the other
questions.expected: One where both people respect, listen and care about each other
questions.memo: In a good relationship, both people respect, listen to and care about each other.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a BAD or unsafe relationship?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a sign of a bad or unsafe relationship?
options: The person makes you feel scared, hurt or controlled
The person treats you with respect
questions.expected: The person makes you feel scared, hurt or controlled
questions.memo: Fear, hurt, control — these are big warning signs. Healthy relationships build us up, not break us down.

questions.question: What is a 'stranger'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a stranger?
questions.expected: A person you don't know
questions.memo: A stranger is someone you don't know. Most strangers are harmless, but you treat unknown people with extra care.

questions.question: A stranger offers you sweets and a ride. The right answer is:
questions.ruby_prompt: A stranger offers you sweets and a ride. What's the right answer?
options: Say no, walk away to a safe place, and tell a trusted adult
Take the ride but leave the sweets
questions.expected: Say no, walk away to a safe place, and tell a trusted adult
questions.memo: Never go anywhere with a stranger, even for sweets or 'help' they ask. Get to a safe place and tell a trusted adult quickly.

questions.question: True or false: A grown-up should NEVER ask a child for help finding a lost dog or directions.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: A grown-up should never ask a child for help finding a lost dog or directions.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Adults ask other ADULTS for help — not lone children. If an adult tries this, it's a warning sign. Walk away and tell a trusted adult.

questions.question: What's a 'safe relationship' with an older person (an adult)?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does a safe relationship with an older person — an adult — look like?
options: They listen, respect your boundaries, and don't ask you to keep secrets
They want to be alone with you a lot
They make you keep secrets from your parents
questions.expected: They listen, respect your boundaries, and don't ask you to keep secrets
questions.memo: Safe adults respect your no, your privacy, and don't isolate you or ask for secrets. The other options are warning signs.

questions.question: An adult tells you 'this is our special secret — don't tell anyone'. You should:
questions.ruby_prompt: An adult says 'this is our special secret — don't tell anyone'. What should you do?
options: Tell a parent or trusted adult straight away
questions.expected: Tell a parent or trusted adult straight away
questions.memo: Safe adults don't ask kids to keep secrets from their parents. This is one of the biggest warning signs. Tell another trusted adult fast.

questions.question: A good friend would NOT:
questions.ruby_prompt: A good friend would NOT do which of these?
options: Make fun of you in front of others to look cool
Stand up for you when others are mean
questions.expected: Make fun of you in front of others to look cool
questions.memo: Real friends don't tear you down to look good. If a 'friend' often does, that relationship needs to change.

questions.question: Which is a BENEFIT of having good relationships?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a benefit of having good relationships in your life?
options: You feel safer, happier and able to ask for help when you need it
questions.expected: You feel safer, happier and able to ask for help when you need it
questions.memo: Good relationships help you feel safer and happier, and you can ask for help when you need it.

questions.question: Lerato's older neighbour gives her gifts and asks her not to tell her mom. What should Lerato do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato's older neighbour gives her gifts and tells her not to tell her mom. What should Lerato do?
options: Tell her mom right away — this is not a safe pattern
questions.expected: Tell her mom right away — this is not a safe pattern
questions.memo: Adults using gifts + secrecy to build a special bond with a child = warning. Telling mom protects Lerato.

questions.question: Which of these helps build a GOOD friendship?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these helps build a good friendship?
options: Honesty, listening, and being there in good and hard times
questions.expected: Honesty, listening, and being there in good and hard times
questions.memo: Good friendships are built on honest words and reliable presence. Gifts and gossip don't last.

questions.question: True or false: It's okay to say no to an adult if they're asking you to do something that feels wrong.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It's okay to say no to an adult if they're asking you to do something that feels wrong.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — even adults can be wrong. Your gut feeling about safety matters. Say no, get to safety, tell a trusted grown-up.

questions.question: Karabo is walking home alone. A car slows down beside her and the driver smiles. What should she do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo is walking home alone. A car slows beside her and the driver smiles. What should she do?
options: Walk fast in the opposite direction and toward people or a shop
Wave back and keep walking past
questions.expected: Walk fast in the opposite direction and toward people or a shop
questions.memo: Cars can't easily turn around. Walking the opposite way buys safety. Heading toward people or a shop adds witnesses and help.

questions.question: Tell me one thing a TRUSTED ADULT in your life does that makes them trustworthy.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one thing a trusted adult in your life does that makes them trustworthy.
questions.expected: They listen to me without judging
questions.memo: A trusted adult listens without judging, keeps you safe and tells you the truth.

questions.question: Put these in order for what to do if a stranger tries to talk to you alone.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what to do if a stranger tries to talk to you when you're alone.
options: Move to where there are people
Walk or run to a safe person (shop owner, police, parent)
Tell a trusted adult about it
questions.expected: Don't get close to them,Move to where there are people,Walk or run to a safe person (shop owner, police, parent),Tell a trusted adult about it
questions.memo: Distance → people → safe adult → tell. This sequence has saved many children.

questions.question: A friend keeps copying your homework and never gives anything back. This is a:
questions.ruby_prompt: A friend keeps copying your homework and never gives anything back. This is a sign of:
options: An unfair relationship — friendships go both ways
questions.expected: An unfair relationship — friendships go both ways
questions.memo: Friendship should go both ways. If only one person gives, it isn't fair.

questions.question: Mpho's friend pushes her to do things she's not comfortable with. The healthy response is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho's friend keeps pushing her to do things she's not comfortable with. What's the healthy response?
options: Say no clearly, and talk to a trusted adult if pushing continues
Just do everything the friend says
questions.expected: Say no clearly, and talk to a trusted adult if pushing continues
questions.memo: Real friends respect your no. If a friend keeps pushing past your no, they're not respecting you — that's not a friendship to keep.

questions.question: Which is the BEST description of a safe adult in your life?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the best description of a safe adult in your life?
options: Someone who listens, respects your no, and won't ask you to keep secrets from other trusted adults
Someone who buys you the most things
questions.expected: Someone who listens, respects your no, and won't ask you to keep secrets from other trusted adults
questions.memo: Safe adults are not defined by gifts, age or job. They're defined by HOW they treat you — with respect, openness and no harmful secrets.

questions.question: Why do good relationships matter for your health?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do good relationships matter for your health?
options: People with good relationships are happier, sleep better and even live longer
questions.expected: People with good relationships are happier, sleep better and even live longer
questions.memo: People with good relationships are happier, sleep better and even live longer.

LS.L5.PSW.T05.title: Discrimination, stereotype and bias
LS.L5.PSW.T05.description: Concepts of discrimination, stereotype and bias as violations of children's rights; how to protect self and others, where to find help, planning a response in own local context.
LS.L5.PSW.T05.recovery_strategy: Define terms simply with everyday examples. Affirm that all people deserve equal treatment under the SA Constitution.

questions.question: What is 'discrimination'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does discrimination mean?
options: Treating someone unfairly because of who they are (race, language, religion, etc.)
questions.expected: Treating someone unfairly because of who they are (race, language, religion, etc.)
questions.memo: Discrimination is treating someone unfairly because of who they are, like their race, language or religion.

questions.question: What is a 'stereotype'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a stereotype?
options: A fixed idea about a group of people that may not be true of individuals
questions.expected: A fixed idea about a group of people that may not be true of individuals
questions.memo: Stereotypes are 'all X people are like Y'. They make individuals invisible. Real people are always more than the group they belong to.

questions.question: What is 'bias'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is bias?
options: Leaning toward or away from something or someone unfairly
questions.expected: Leaning toward or away from something or someone unfairly
questions.memo: Bias is unfairly favouring one side or person over another. We can have biases without noticing.

questions.question: Which is an example of discrimination?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is an example of discrimination?
options: A child is refused entry to a club because of the colour of their skin
A child wins a prize for hard work
questions.expected: A child is refused entry to a club because of the colour of their skin
questions.memo: Keeping a child out of a club because of their skin colour is discrimination. It is against the Constitution.

questions.question: Which is an example of a STEREOTYPE?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a stereotype?
questions.expected: 'Boys don't cry'
questions.memo: 'Boys don't cry' is a stereotype: a fixed idea about a whole group. The others just say what happened.

questions.question: True or false: Discrimination is a violation of children's rights.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Discrimination is a violation of children's rights.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Every child has the right to be treated equally. Discrimination breaks that right.

questions.question: Sipho hears a classmate use a racist word about another child. What should he do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho hears a classmate use a racist word about another child. What should he do?
options: Tell the classmate that's not okay and tell a teacher
questions.expected: Tell the classmate that's not okay and tell a teacher
