questions.memo: Speaking up against racism is powerful. Telling a teacher means an adult can deal with it properly.

questions.question: Which document in SA protects everyone from discrimination?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which big document in South Africa protects everyone from discrimination?
options: The Constitution and the Bill of Rights
questions.expected: The Constitution and the Bill of Rights
questions.memo: The Bill of Rights, in the Constitution, says everyone is equal and protects us from unfair treatment.

questions.question: A bias can be:
questions.ruby_prompt: A bias can be:
options: Either positive (favouring) or negative (disliking) without good reason
questions.expected: Either positive (favouring) or negative (disliking) without good reason
questions.memo: Bias can go either way — favouring people like you OR disliking those who aren't. Both are bias.

questions.question: Lerato says: 'Girls can't play football.' This is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato says, 'Girls can't play football.' What is this?
options: A stereotype — many girls and women play football well
questions.expected: A stereotype — many girls and women play football well
questions.memo: That is a stereotype. Banyana Banyana and many other girls and women play football well.

questions.question: If you see another child being discriminated against, you can:
questions.ruby_prompt: If you see another child being discriminated against, what can you do?
options: Stand by them, tell an adult, and don't join the discriminating
questions.expected: Stand by them, tell an adult, and don't join the discriminating
questions.memo: Bystanders make a huge difference. Standing with the person, telling an adult, refusing to join in — all help.

questions.question: True or false: Everyone has SOME biases — even kind people.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Everyone has some biases — even kind people.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: We all soak up ideas from family, media and society. The work isn't to be free of bias — it's to notice it and challenge it in ourselves.

questions.question: Karabo is told she 'can't be a scientist because she's a girl'. The truth is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo is told she can't be a scientist because she's a girl. What's the truth?
options: Girls and women can and do become scientists in every field
questions.expected: Girls and women can and do become scientists in every field
questions.memo: Many of the world's top scientists are women — and SA has its own famous women scientists like Quarraisha Abdool Karim. Stereotypes are not facts.

questions.question: Where can a child in SA find help if their rights are being violated?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where can a child in South Africa find help if their rights are being violated?
options: Childline 116, a school counsellor, the SA Human Rights Commission, or a trusted adult
Only the school principal can help
questions.expected: Childline 116, a school counsellor, the SA Human Rights Commission, or a trusted adult
questions.memo: Help is real and free. Childline 116 (24-hour), school counsellor, SAHRC (rights body), and any trusted adult are all paths.

questions.question: Put these steps in order if you experience discrimination at school.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these steps in order if you experience discrimination at school.
options: Notice what happened and how it made you feel
Tell a teacher or counsellor you trust
Ask for it to be dealt with — there are school policies
Talk to a parent or Childline if it continues
questions.expected: Notice what happened and how it made you feel,Tell a teacher or counsellor you trust,Ask for it to be dealt with — there are school policies,Talk to a parent or Childline if it continues
questions.memo: Notice → tell → ask for action → escalate. Every step makes the next easier.

questions.question: Tell me one example of a stereotype you have heard.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one stereotype you have heard about a group of people.
questions.expected: Boys don't cry
questions.memo: Good answers: any 'all X are Y' statement — 'boys are tough', 'girls like pink', 'old people are slow', etc. Once we notice a stereotype, we can challenge it.

questions.question: Which is a way to PROTECT yourself and others from discrimination?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to protect yourself and others from discrimination?
options: Learn the Bill of Rights, speak up kindly, and ask trusted adults for help
Make fun of those who report it
questions.expected: Learn the Bill of Rights, speak up kindly, and ask trusted adults for help
questions.memo: Knowing your rights gives you confidence to act. Calm speaking-up + adult help beats silence or revenge.

questions.question: Why is the apartheid history important to know when learning about discrimination in SA?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is apartheid history important to know when learning about discrimination in SA?
options: South Africa lived through extreme legal discrimination — knowing this helps us never go back
questions.expected: South Africa lived through extreme legal discrimination — knowing this helps us never go back
questions.memo: Apartheid was discrimination written into the law. Knowing about it helps make sure it never comes back.

questions.question: Which is a positive action a class can take to reduce discrimination at school?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a positive action a class can take to reduce discrimination at school?
options: Make a class promise to speak up when discrimination happens
Form separate groups by race or language
questions.expected: Make a class promise to speak up when discrimination happens
questions.memo: Class agreements set a culture. When the whole class promises to speak up, individuals feel braver. Cultures shift this way.

questions.question: The most powerful answer to discrimination is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most powerful answer to discrimination?
options: Treating every person as equal in dignity and worth
questions.expected: Treating every person as equal in dignity and worth
questions.memo: The strongest answer is to treat every person as equal and worthy of respect.

LS.L5.PSW.T06.title: Child abuse
LS.L5.PSW.T06.description: Forms of child abuse (physical and emotional), effects on personal health, strategies to deal with abuse, where to get help and report abuse.
LS.L5.PSW.T06.recovery_strategy: Always reinforce: abuse is NEVER the child's fault. Telling a trusted adult or Childline 116 is the bravest, smartest move. Never describe abuse in graphic terms.

questions.question: What is 'child abuse'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is child abuse?
options: When a grown-up or older person hurts a child on purpose — physically or emotionally
When a child loses a sports match
questions.expected: When a grown-up or older person hurts a child on purpose — physically or emotionally
questions.memo: Child abuse is on-purpose harm to a child — hitting, hurting, scaring, or threatening. It is against the law and against children's rights.

questions.question: Which is a form of PHYSICAL abuse?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a form of physical abuse?
options: Hitting, shaking or burning a child
Asking a child to wash dishes
Asking a child to make their bed
questions.expected: Hitting, shaking or burning a child
questions.memo: Physical abuse is hurting a child's body, like hitting, shaking or burning. Chores and homework are normal.

questions.question: Which is a form of EMOTIONAL abuse?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a form of emotional abuse?
options: Repeatedly insulting, scaring or rejecting a child
Telling a child you love them
questions.expected: Repeatedly insulting, scaring or rejecting a child
questions.memo: Emotional abuse is hurting a child with words and actions, again and again, like insults, threats or saying they aren't wanted.

questions.question: True or false: Child abuse is NEVER the child's fault.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Child abuse is never the child's fault.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Always true. Children are never to blame for being abused. Abuse is the responsibility of the abuser, not the child.

questions.question: Where can a child in South Africa call to report abuse, for free, day or night?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where can a child in South Africa call to report abuse — free, day or night?
questions.expected: Childline 116
questions.memo: Childline 116 is free from any phone in SA. Trained counsellors listen and help. They can also help with police or social workers.

questions.question: If a child is being abused, the most important first step is:
questions.ruby_prompt: If a child is being abused, what's the most important first step?
options: Tell a trusted adult (teacher, neighbour, parent of a friend) or call Childline 116
questions.expected: Tell a trusted adult (teacher, neighbour, parent of a friend) or call Childline 116
questions.memo: Telling breaks the silence that keeps abuse going. There are people whose JOB it is to help — telling them is brave, not wrong.

questions.question: Effects of abuse on personal health can include:
questions.ruby_prompt: Effects of abuse on a child's personal health can include what?
options: Trouble sleeping, sadness, fear, and physical harm
questions.expected: Trouble sleeping, sadness, fear, and physical harm
questions.memo: Abuse hurts the whole child — body, sleep, feelings, school. With help and care, healing is possible. That's why telling matters.

questions.question: A friend tells you they are being hurt at home and asks you not to tell. You should:
questions.ruby_prompt: A friend tells you they are being hurt at home but asks you not to tell anyone. What should you do?
options: Tell a trusted adult anyway — this is one secret that protecting saves lives
questions.expected: Tell a trusted adult anyway — this is one secret that protecting saves lives
questions.memo: Real friendship is keeping your friend safe — even if they're scared of telling. A trusted adult or Childline can help both of you.

questions.question: True or false: When a child tells about abuse, they should be believed and helped.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: When a child tells about abuse, they should be believed and helped.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Children almost never make up abuse. Believing a child who speaks up is the start of helping them.

questions.question: Which is a TRUSTED ADULT a child could tell about abuse?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which adult could a child tell about abuse?
options: A teacher, school counsellor, family doctor, religious leader, or a friend's parent
Only their own parents (even if a parent is the abuser)
questions.expected: A teacher, school counsellor, family doctor, religious leader, or a friend's parent
questions.memo: Trusted adults are everywhere. If the abuse is at home, the adult to tell is NOT at home — try a teacher, counsellor or friend's parent.

questions.question: Sipho's older cousin keeps slapping him when no one is looking. What should Sipho do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's older cousin keeps slapping him when no one is looking. What should Sipho do?
options: Tell a parent, teacher or call Childline 116 — this is abuse
Wait for the cousin to grow up
questions.expected: Tell a parent, teacher or call Childline 116 — this is abuse
questions.memo: Hitting a child IS abuse — even from family. Sipho deserves safety. Telling brings the help that stops the cycle.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for what to do if you are being abused.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these steps in the right order for what to do if you are being abused.
options: Get to a safe place if you can
Tell a trusted adult or call Childline 116
Look after yourself with the help of caring grown-ups
questions.expected: Get to a safe place if you can,Tell a trusted adult or call Childline 116,Keep telling until someone helps,Look after yourself with the help of caring grown-ups
questions.memo: Safety → tell → keep telling → heal. Sometimes the first adult doesn't act — KEEP TELLING. Help is real.

questions.question: Which sentence is TRUE about abuse?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is true about abuse?
options: Abuse happens in all kinds of families — rich or poor, big or small
questions.expected: Abuse happens in all kinds of families — rich or poor, big or small
questions.memo: Abuse crosses every line of money, race, religion and language. That's why every child needs to know how to ask for help.

questions.question: Karabo is being abused by an adult at home. She is scared to tell. The most important thing she needs to know is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo is being abused by an adult at home. She's scared to tell. What's the most important thing she needs to know?
options: It is not her fault, she is not alone, and there are adults whose JOB is to help her
questions.expected: It is not her fault, she is not alone, and there are adults whose JOB is to help her
questions.memo: Three truths bigger than the fear: not your fault, not alone, real help exists. Hold onto them. Call Childline 116 (free).

questions.question: True or false: Insults and threats are abuse, even when nobody hits anyone.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Insults and threats are abuse, even when nobody is hit.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Constant insults and threats are abuse too. Children deserve to feel safe inside as well.

questions.question: Tell me a phone number a child in SA can call for help with abuse.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me a phone number a child in South Africa can call for help with abuse.
questions.expected: 116 — Childline South Africa
questions.memo: Childline 116. Free. 24 hours. Trained to listen and help. Memorise this number — it can save a friend's life one day.

questions.question: If the first adult you tell doesn't help, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: If the first adult you tell doesn't help, you should:
options: Tell another trusted adult — and another, until someone helps
questions.expected: Tell another trusted adult — and another, until someone helps
questions.memo: Some adults react badly to hard news. That's on them, not you. KEEP telling. The right help is out there.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT abuse — it's normal childhood?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is NOT abuse — it's just normal childhood?
options: Being asked to help with chores at home
Being hit hard until you bruise
questions.expected: Being asked to help with chores at home
questions.memo: Helping with chores is normal. Being hit, shouted at every day, or locked away is abuse.

questions.question: Mpho hears a child scream in pain next door, regularly. What should Mpho do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho hears a child scream in pain next door regularly. What should Mpho do?
options: Tell a parent or teacher — they can report it to a social worker
questions.expected: Tell a parent or teacher — they can report it to a social worker
questions.memo: When you hear repeated screams of pain, a child may need help. Telling an adult can save that child. Social workers can step in.

questions.question: What is the SAFEST first thing to remember if you are being abused?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the safest first thing to remember if you are being abused?
options: You are not alone, it is not your fault, and there is real help — Childline 116
questions.expected: You are not alone, it is not your fault, and there is real help — Childline 116
questions.memo: These four words can change a life: not alone, not my fault, real help. Repeat them. Call Childline 116. Tell.

LS.L5.PSW.T07.title: Dealing with violent situations
LS.L5.PSW.T07.description: Identifying potential violent situations at home, school and community; responding effectively; ways to avoid and protect oneself, where to find help.
LS.L5.PSW.T07.recovery_strategy: Priority is always GET AWAY SAFELY, not confront. Reinforce: telling a trusted adult or police is the right action. Don't romanticise being brave.

questions.question: What is a 'violent situation'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a violent situation?
options: A situation where someone might or does get physically hurt
questions.expected: A situation where someone might or does get physically hurt
questions.memo: A violent situation is one where someone might get hurt, like a fight or a robbery.

questions.question: When you see a fight starting, the SAFEST first thing is:
questions.ruby_prompt: When you see a fight starting, what's the safest first thing to do?
options: Get away to a safe place — don't try to break it up yourself
questions.expected: Get away to a safe place — don't try to break it up yourself
questions.memo: Untrained people who jump in often get hurt too. Safety first. Then tell an adult who can stop it properly.

questions.question: If someone tries to take your phone or bag on the street, the safest move is:
questions.ruby_prompt: If someone tries to take your phone or bag on the street, what is the safest move?
options: Give it up — your safety is worth more than any object
questions.expected: Give it up — your safety is worth more than any object
questions.memo: Things can be replaced. You cannot. Police agree: hand it over, get to safety, and report it.

questions.question: Where can you usually find help in a public place during a violent situation?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where can you usually find help in a public place when something violent is happening?
options: A shop, a police station, a security guard, or a busy place with many people
questions.expected: A shop, a police station, a security guard, or a busy place with many people
questions.memo: People = safety. Empty places = danger. Run toward where there are witnesses and adults.

questions.question: What is the SA police emergency number?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is the SA police emergency number?
questions.memo: 10111 = SA Police. 10177 = ambulance. 112 from a mobile phone connects to emergency services. Worth memorising.

questions.question: True or false: It is brave to fight any attacker by yourself.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It is brave to fight any attacker by yourself.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Movies make it look brave; real life makes it dangerous. Getting away and getting help is the wise move.

questions.question: At home, if you hear adults fighting violently, the safest place for a child is:
questions.ruby_prompt: At home, if adults are fighting violently, where is the safest place for a child?
options: Go to a safe room or neighbour, and call a trusted adult or Childline 116
Try to break up the fight
Hide in the middle of it
questions.expected: Go to a safe room or neighbour, and call a trusted adult or Childline 116
questions.memo: Children must NEVER try to break up adult fights. Get to a safe space — locked room, neighbour, outside — and call for help.

questions.question: Lerato sees a robbery happening across the street. What should she do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato sees a robbery happening across the street. What should she do?
options: Move away to safety and call 10111 or tell an adult to call
questions.expected: Move away to safety and call 10111 or tell an adult to call
questions.memo: Witnesses can describe what happened to police later. But first, safety. Move away. Then call.

questions.question: Which is a way to AVOID being in a violent situation?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to avoid being in a violent situation?
options: Walk in groups, in busy streets, and during the day when possible
Walk alone late at night in quiet places
Wear loose jewellery as a target
questions.expected: Walk in groups, in busy streets, and during the day when possible
questions.memo: Most crime targets the vulnerable — alone, dark places, late hours. Group + busy + daylight is the safer mix.

questions.question: If you witness violence at school, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: If you witness violence at school, what should you do?
options: Tell a teacher or principal immediately
questions.expected: Tell a teacher or principal immediately
questions.memo: Teachers can stop violence faster than children can. Telling = action. Watching = the violence continues.

questions.question: True or false: Carrying a weapon to protect yourself is the best response.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Carrying a weapon at school to protect yourself is the best response.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Weapons at school are dangerous and illegal. They often make children targets and get used against them. Safety = adults + plans + avoiding hot spots.

questions.question: Put these in order for what to do if you're attacked.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what to do if you are attacked.
options: Move toward people or a safe place
Tell a trusted adult or call 10111
Talk to a counsellor afterwards about your feelings
questions.expected: Give up belongings if asked,Move toward people or a safe place,Tell a trusted adult or call 10111,Talk to a counsellor afterwards about your feelings
questions.memo: Give up your things if asked. Get to a safe place near people. Tell an adult or call 10111. Later, talk to a counsellor about how you feel.

questions.question: Karabo's neighbourhood has a lot of violence. The best thing for her family to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's neighbourhood has a lot of violence. What's the best thing her family can do?
options: Plan safe routes, keep doors locked, know neighbours, and contact community safety groups
questions.expected: Plan safe routes, keep doors locked, know neighbours, and contact community safety groups
questions.memo: Plan safe routes, lock doors, know the neighbours, and join community safety groups. Together they keep a family safer.

questions.question: Sipho is being asked to join a gang. What should he do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho is being asked to join a gang. What should he do?
options: Say no, tell a trusted adult, and stay close to safe friends
questions.expected: Say no, tell a trusted adult, and stay close to safe friends
questions.memo: Gangs lead to violence, prison, and death. Saying no is the only safe answer. A trusted adult or social worker can help with the pressure.

questions.question: Tell me one safety rule for walking to school.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one safety rule for walking to school.
questions.expected: Walk with friends, not alone
questions.memo: Walk with friends, not alone. Use main roads, and tell a parent your route.

questions.question: Mpho sees a gun on the floor at her school. What should she do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho sees a gun on the floor at her school. What should she do?
options: Don't touch it. Move away. Tell a teacher straight away
questions.expected: Don't touch it. Move away. Tell a teacher straight away
questions.memo: Guns hurt and kill — even by 'accident'. Don't touch. Move away. Get an adult. That sequence saves lives.

questions.question: After a frightening event, it's normal to feel:
questions.ruby_prompt: After a frightening or violent event, it's normal to feel what?
options: Shaken, scared, sad or angry for some time afterwards — talking to a counsellor helps
questions.expected: Shaken, scared, sad or angry for some time afterwards — talking to a counsellor helps
questions.memo: Strong feelings after a scare are normal — your body and mind processing it. School counsellors and Childline (116) can help.

questions.question: Which sign warns that a situation might get violent?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which sign might warn that a situation could get violent?
options: People shouting, threatening or fists clenched
questions.expected: People shouting, threatening or fists clenched
questions.memo: Early warning signs: raised voices, threats, fists, blocked exits, alcohol involved. Notice them and move away early.

questions.question: Why is it important to talk to someone after a violent event?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to talk to someone after a violent event?
options: Sharing helps you process the fear and stops it from getting stuck
questions.expected: Sharing helps you process the fear and stops it from getting stuck
questions.memo: Untalked-about fear can linger for years. A counsellor or trusted adult helps the feelings move through, not stay stuck.

questions.question: What's the MOST IMPORTANT rule about violent situations?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most important rule about violent situations?
options: Get yourself to safety first, then get help — things can be replaced; you cannot
Always try to be a hero
questions.expected: Get yourself to safety first, then get help — things can be replaced; you cannot
questions.memo: Safety first, help second. This rule is from real police and rescuers. Your life is worth more than any object or moment of pride.

LS.L5.PSW.T08.title: Issues of age and gender in cultural contexts
LS.L5.PSW.T08.description: Relationships between elders and children in different SA cultural contexts; responsibilities of boys and girls; contributions of women and men.
LS.L5.PSW.T08.recovery_strategy: Respect cultural traditions while affirming the SA Constitution's equality. Help the learner see both: the value of elders' wisdom AND the equal dignity of girls and boys.

questions.question: In many SA cultures, what is shown to elders (older people)?
questions.ruby_prompt: In many South African cultures, what is shown to elders?
options: Respect — they are seen as keepers of wisdom and tradition
questions.expected: Respect — they are seen as keepers of wisdom and tradition
questions.memo: In many South African cultures, elders are respected because of their wisdom and experience.

questions.question: Which is a way to show respect to an elder?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these shows respect to an elder?
options: Greeting them first and listening when they speak
questions.expected: Greeting them first and listening when they speak
questions.memo: Greet elders first and listen when they speak. That shows respect.

questions.question: True or false: Boys and girls have equal rights under the SA Constitution.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Boys and girls have equal rights under the SA Constitution.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — the SA Constitution guarantees gender equality. Girls and boys may do the same jobs and have the same chances in life.

questions.question: Which is a stereotype about gender?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a gender stereotype?
options: 'Some girls play rugby and some don't'
questions.expected: 'Girls don't play rugby'
questions.memo: Banning girls from a sport based on gender is a stereotype. The Springbok Women prove it's untrue.

questions.question: Which is a stereotype about boys?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a stereotype about boys?
questions.expected: 'Boys don't cook'
questions.memo: Many world-famous chefs are men. The stereotype that boys don't cook is just that — a stereotype.

questions.question: In SA, MEN and WOMEN can do which kinds of work?
questions.ruby_prompt: In South Africa, which kinds of work can men and women do?
options: The same kinds — there are female doctors, engineers, taxi drivers; male nurses, teachers, chefs
There are completely separate jobs by gender
questions.expected: The same kinds — there are female doctors, engineers, taxi drivers; male nurses, teachers, chefs
questions.memo: Men and women can do the same jobs. There are women doctors and taxi drivers, and men who are nurses and chefs.

questions.question: Name a South African woman who has contributed greatly to the country:
questions.ruby_prompt: Name a South African woman who has contributed greatly to the country.
options: Winnie Madikizela-Mandela, Albertina Sisulu, Charlotte Maxeke
Only foreign women have done this
questions.expected: Winnie Madikizela-Mandela, Albertina Sisulu, Charlotte Maxeke
questions.memo: Many SA women have shaped our country — in freedom struggle, science, business, sports. Knowing their names matters.

questions.question: Which is a way an ELDER can teach a younger person?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way an elder can teach a younger person?
options: Telling stories from their life and the past
questions.expected: Telling stories from their life and the past
questions.memo: Elders can teach by telling stories from their life and from long ago.

questions.question: True or false: Both boys and girls can take part in chores at home.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Both boys and girls can take part in chores at home.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Cooking, cleaning, fetching water, looking after younger siblings — these are family tasks, not 'girl' or 'boy' tasks.

questions.question: In some traditional homes, what is the SHARED responsibility of all children?
questions.ruby_prompt: In many traditional SA homes, what's a shared responsibility of all children?
options: Respecting elders, helping with family tasks, doing well at school
questions.expected: Respecting elders, helping with family tasks, doing well at school
questions.memo: Across SA cultures, children share these core duties — respect, help, learn. Specific tasks may vary, but the values overlap.

questions.question: Lerato wants to be an engineer. Her grandmother says, 'That's a man's job.' What's true?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato wants to become an engineer. Her grandmother says, 'That's a man's job.' What is true?
options: South Africa has many women engineers — Lerato can absolutely become one
questions.expected: South Africa has many women engineers — Lerato can absolutely become one
questions.memo: Times have changed. Many SA women are engineers, scientists, surgeons. Lerato can pursue her dream — and respect her grandmother while doing so.

questions.question: Why is it important to learn FROM elders?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to learn from elders?
options: They've lived through things we can learn from without making the same mistakes
questions.expected: They've lived through things we can learn from without making the same mistakes
questions.memo: Elders' life experience is a free gift to younger people. They've seen droughts, wars, freedom, change — wisdom that books can't fully capture.

questions.question: Karabo's brother says girls 'shouldn't be loud or strong'. What's the truth?
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's brother says girls 'shouldn't be loud or strong.' What's the truth?
options: Girls can be loud or quiet, strong or gentle — whatever they choose, just like boys
questions.expected: Girls can be loud or quiet, strong or gentle — whatever they choose, just like boys
questions.memo: Personality is personal — not a gender rule. Some girls are quiet, some loud; same for boys. All are okay.

questions.question: Which is a healthy view of age and gender in SA?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a healthy view of age and gender in SA?
options: Respect for elders + equal rights for all genders
questions.expected: Respect for elders + equal rights for all genders
questions.memo: We can respect our elders and also believe all genders have equal rights.

questions.question: Tell me one task at home that BOTH boys and girls can do.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one task at home that both boys and girls can do.
questions.expected: Washing dishes
questions.memo: Good answers: washing dishes, sweeping, cooking, looking after siblings, doing laundry, gardening. Any home task can be shared.

questions.question: Sipho's class is told 'only boys lift the heavy tables'. What's a fairer rule?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's class is told 'only boys lift the heavy tables.' What would be fairer?
options: Anyone strong enough can help — not based on gender
questions.expected: Anyone strong enough can help — not based on gender
questions.memo: A fairer rule is that anyone strong enough can help. Strength depends on the person, not on being a boy or girl.

questions.question: When younger and older family members work together, the result is often:
questions.ruby_prompt: When younger and older family members work together, what's the result often?
options: Both learn — young get wisdom, elders get help and new ideas
questions.expected: Both learn — young get wisdom, elders get help and new ideas
questions.memo: Both learn. Young people get wisdom, and elders get help and new ideas.

questions.question: True or false: Men can be loving caregivers to children too.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Men can be loving caregivers to children too.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Fathers, uncles, grandfathers, male teachers — men nurture children every day. It's part of being human.

questions.question: What's a respectful way to disagree with an elder?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a respectful way to disagree with an elder?
options: Listen first, ask questions, then share your view calmly
questions.expected: Listen first, ask questions, then share your view calmly
questions.memo: Listen first, ask questions, then calmly share what you think. You can disagree and still be respectful.

questions.question: The SA Constitution says about gender:
questions.ruby_prompt: What does the SA Constitution say about gender?
options: Everyone is equal regardless of gender — no discrimination is allowed
questions.expected: Everyone is equal regardless of gender — no discrimination is allowed
questions.memo: The Constitution says everyone is equal, whatever their gender. Unfair treatment is not allowed.

LS.L5.PSW.T09.title: Festivals and customs of religions in South Africa
LS.L5.PSW.T09.description: Festivals and customs from a variety of religions in South Africa.
LS.L5.PSW.T09.recovery_strategy: Treat each festival with equal respect. Aim is recognition and curiosity, not deep theology. Use SA examples where possible.

questions.question: What is a 'religious festival'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a religious festival?
options: A special celebration that is part of a religion
questions.expected: A special celebration that is part of a religion
questions.memo: A religious festival is a special celebration that is part of a religion.

questions.question: Christmas is a major festival for which religion?
questions.ruby_prompt: Christmas is a major festival for which religion?
questions.expected: Christianity
questions.memo: Christmas is a Christian festival. It celebrates the birth of Jesus.

questions.question: Eid is a festival for which religion?
questions.ruby_prompt: Eid is a festival for which religion?
questions.expected: Islam
questions.memo: Eid is a Muslim festival. One Eid marks the end of Ramadan, a month of fasting.

questions.question: Diwali (the Festival of Lights) is celebrated by:
questions.ruby_prompt: Diwali — the Festival of Lights — is celebrated by which religion?
questions.expected: Hindus
questions.memo: Diwali, the Festival of Lights, is celebrated by Hindus.

questions.question: Passover (Pesach) is celebrated by:
questions.ruby_prompt: Passover, also called Pesach, is celebrated by which religion?
questions.expected: Jewish people
questions.memo: Passover is celebrated by Jewish people. It remembers their escape from slavery in Egypt.

questions.question: True or false: SA has many religions and many religious festivals throughout the year.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: South Africa has many religions and many religious festivals throughout the year.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. South Africa has many religions, so there are festivals all through the year.

questions.question: Ramadan is a special month in Islam when Muslims:
questions.ruby_prompt: Ramadan is a special month in Islam when Muslims:
options: Fast from food and drink during daylight hours
questions.expected: Fast from food and drink during daylight hours
questions.memo: During Ramadan, grown-up Muslims don't eat or drink from sunrise to sunset.

questions.question: Easter, in Christianity, celebrates:
questions.ruby_prompt: Easter, in Christianity, celebrates what?
questions.expected: The resurrection of Jesus
questions.memo: At Easter, Christians celebrate Jesus rising from the dead.

questions.question: Vesak (Wesak) is a festival celebrated by:
questions.ruby_prompt: Vesak, sometimes called Wesak, is a festival of which religion?
questions.expected: Buddhists
questions.memo: Vesak is a Buddhist festival. It celebrates the Buddha.

questions.question: African Religion includes ceremonies to:
questions.ruby_prompt: African Religion includes ceremonies to do what?
options: Honour ancestors and important life events
questions.expected: Honour ancestors and important life events
questions.memo: African Religion has ceremonies to honour the ancestors and mark big life events, like births and weddings.

questions.question: Why do many religions celebrate festivals?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do many religions celebrate festivals?
options: To remember important events and share them with family and community
questions.expected: To remember important events and share them with family and community
questions.memo: Festivals help people remember important events and share them with family and community.

questions.question: When a classmate is fasting for Ramadan, you can show respect by:
questions.ruby_prompt: When a classmate is fasting for Ramadan, you can show respect by:
options: Not making a big show of eating in front of them and asking what helps them
Eating extra food in front of them
Pretending to fast yourself when you're not
questions.expected: Not making a big show of eating in front of them and asking what helps them
questions.memo: Small kindnesses go a long way — being quiet about your own food, asking what they need. Respect doesn't require sharing the belief.

questions.question: True or false: Knowing about other religions' festivals helps us live together better.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Knowing about other religions' festivals helps us live together better.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Understanding our neighbours' celebrations helps us live together well.

questions.question: Hanukkah, the Jewish Festival of Lights, is celebrated by:
questions.ruby_prompt: Hanukkah, the Jewish Festival of Lights, is celebrated by lighting what?
options: A menorah — a nine-branched candleholder, over eight nights
A single candle for one hour
questions.expected: A menorah — a nine-branched candleholder, over eight nights
questions.memo: Hanukkah lasts eight nights. One candle is added each night on the menorah, marking the miracle of light lasting eight days.

questions.question: Which is a common feature across MANY religious festivals?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a common feature across many religious festivals?
options: Gathering with family, sharing food, prayer or reflection
questions.expected: Gathering with family, sharing food, prayer or reflection
questions.memo: Many festivals include family, sharing food, and prayer or quiet thinking.

questions.question: Match festival to religion: Diwali
questions.ruby_prompt: Pictures: a lit-up oil lamp (diya), a Christmas tree, a crescent moon and star, a Star of David. Which picture shows Diwali?
questions.context: Pictures: a lit-up oil lamp (diya), a Christmas tree, a crescent moon and star, a Star of David
questions.expected: Lit-up oil lamp (diya)
questions.memo: Small oil lamps called diyas are a sign of Diwali. They stand for light winning over darkness.

questions.question: Lerato's friend invites her to celebrate Eid. The kind thing to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato's friend invites her to celebrate Eid with her family. What's the kind thing to do?
options: Go with respect, dress modestly, and learn about it
Eat all the food without thanks
questions.expected: Go with respect, dress modestly, and learn about it
questions.memo: Lerato should go with respect, dress modestly and learn about it. Saying thank you makes it special.

questions.question: Tell me one religious festival you know of and what it celebrates.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one religious festival you know of and what it celebrates.
questions.expected: Christmas — the birth of Jesus in Christianity
questions.memo: Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus. Eid, Diwali and Passover are other festivals.

questions.question: What is the Baha'i Naw-Rúz festival?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is the Baha'i Naw-Rúz festival?
options: The Baha'i New Year, celebrated around 21 March
questions.expected: The Baha'i New Year, celebrated around 21 March
questions.memo: Naw-Rúz means 'new day'. It's the Baha'i (and Persian) New Year, marking the start of spring in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.question: Why might a school celebrate or learn about many religious festivals?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why might a school choose to celebrate or learn about many religious festivals?
options: To respect every learner's background and build understanding across the community
To pick one religion as best
questions.expected: To respect every learner's background and build understanding across the community
questions.memo: When a school honours many traditions, every child feels seen — and all children learn to see each other clearly. That is the SA we want.

LS.L5.PSW.T10.title: Safety measures at home and the environment
LS.L5.PSW.T10.description: Harmful household products and medication, fire safety.
LS.L5.PSW.T10.recovery_strategy: Concrete rules save lives. Build the learner's mental safety checklist around chemicals, medicines, fire and electricity.

questions.question: Which is a harmful household product?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a harmful household product?
questions.expected: Bleach or strong drain cleaner
questions.memo: Bleach and drain cleaner are harmful. They can burn skin and eyes, and poison you if swallowed.

questions.question: Where should medicines be stored?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where should medicines be stored at home?
options: Out of reach of young children — high up and locked if possible
On the floor next to the toys
questions.expected: Out of reach of young children — high up and locked if possible
questions.memo: Many children are poisoned each year from medicines they thought were sweets. Lock them up. Out of reach.

questions.question: If you swallow something poisonous, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you swallow something poisonous, what should you do?
options: Tell an adult immediately and call the Poisons Information Centre or 10177
Wait to see if you feel sick
questions.expected: Tell an adult immediately and call the Poisons Information Centre or 10177
questions.memo: Speed saves lives in poisoning. SA Poisons Information Centre: 0861 555 777. Ambulance: 10177. Don't wait.

questions.question: True or false: Medicine should always be taken from an adult, not by yourself.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Medicine should always be given to children by an adult, not taken by the child alone.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Even safe medicines can hurt at the wrong dose. Adults give children's medicine — always.

questions.question: What should you do FIRST if a small fire starts in the kitchen?
questions.ruby_prompt: What should you do first if a small fire starts in the kitchen?
options: Get everyone out and call for help (10177 or fire service)
Pour water on an oil fire
Watch it to see what happens
questions.expected: Get everyone out and call for help (10177 or fire service)
questions.memo: People first. Get out, get help. Don't fight a fire unless you are TRAINED and it's tiny.

questions.question: True or false: It is safe to put water on a burning paraffin (kerosene) fire.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It is safe to put water on a burning paraffin fire.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Water on paraffin or oil makes the fire EXPLODE outward. Smother it (a heavy lid) or use sand. Better — get out and call for help.

questions.question: Sipho sees an open container of paraffin near a fire. The safest thing to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho sees an open container of paraffin standing close to a cooking fire. What's the safest thing to do?
options: Move it far away from the fire — paraffin can catch fire easily
Pour it on the fire to make it bigger
questions.expected: Move it far away from the fire — paraffin can catch fire easily
questions.memo: Paraffin and other fuels catch fire easily. Keep them well away from flames. Many SA shack fires start this way.

questions.question: Which is a fire safety rule for the home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a fire safety rule for the home?
options: Leave the stove on all day
Light candles in bedrooms before sleeping
questions.expected: Never leave food cooking unattended
questions.memo: Unattended cooking is the leading cause of house fires. Stay in the kitchen while cooking.

questions.question: If your clothes catch fire, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: If your clothes ever catch fire, you should:
options: STOP, DROP and ROLL — to smother the flames
Run as fast as you can
questions.expected: STOP, DROP and ROLL — to smother the flames
questions.memo: STOP (don't run — running feeds the fire). DROP (to the ground). ROLL (to put it out). Cover your face. Then get help.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for what to do if your house is on fire.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what to do if your house is on fire.
options: Close doors behind you to slow the fire
questions.expected: Get everyone out fast,Stay low — smoke rises,Close doors behind you to slow the fire,Call 10177 from outside
questions.memo: Out → low (smoke kills more than flames) → close doors to slow the spread → call from outside. Never go back in for stuff.

questions.question: Why are matches and lighters dangerous for younger children?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are matches and lighters dangerous for younger children?
options: A small flame can start a big fire that can hurt people and burn down homes
questions.expected: A small flame can start a big fire that can hurt people and burn down homes
questions.memo: Matches and lighters belong with adults — never with toddlers or as toys. House fires often start with a child's curiosity.

questions.question: Which is a hidden danger of paraffin stoves and candles?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a hidden danger of paraffin stoves and candles?
options: They can be knocked over and start a fire
questions.expected: They can be knocked over and start a fire
questions.memo: Paraffin stoves and candles can be knocked over and start a fire.

questions.question: True or false: You should never plug too many appliances into one socket.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: You should never plug too many appliances into one wall socket.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Too many plugs in one socket can start an electrical fire.

questions.question: Karabo finds an old bottle with no label under the kitchen sink. She should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo finds an old bottle with no label under the kitchen sink. She should:
options: Not touch it — show an adult and let them handle it
Drink it to find out what's inside
questions.expected: Not touch it — show an adult and let them handle it
questions.memo: Don't touch it. A bottle with no label could hold anything. Show an adult.

questions.question: Which is a safer way to use electricity?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is the safer way to use electricity at home?
options: Keep cords away from water and don't touch sockets with wet hands
Use plugs while standing in water
questions.expected: Keep cords away from water and don't touch sockets with wet hands
questions.memo: Water + electricity = severe shock or death. Dry hands. Cords out of water. Never poke things into sockets.

questions.question: Tell me one fire safety rule.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one fire safety rule.
questions.expected: Never leave a stove on without watching it
questions.memo: Never leave a stove on without watching it. Don't keep candles in bedrooms.

questions.question: If a small grease (oil) fire starts in a pan, the BEST move is:
questions.ruby_prompt: If a small grease fire starts in a pan on the stove, what's the best move?
options: Turn off the heat and cover the pan with a lid to smother it
Pick the pan up and run
questions.expected: Turn off the heat and cover the pan with a lid to smother it
questions.memo: Smothering removes the air the fire needs. Water turns oil into a fireball. Lid = safe. Water on oil = disaster.

questions.question: Which is a sign of carbon monoxide danger from a stove?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a sign of carbon monoxide danger from a stove?
options: Headaches, dizziness, sleepiness in everyone at home
questions.expected: Headaches, dizziness, sleepiness in everyone at home
questions.memo: If everyone at home gets headaches, feels dizzy or sleepy near a stove, it could be a deadly gas. Get outside.

questions.question: What is the SA fire/ambulance number?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the SA emergency number for fire and ambulance?
questions.memo: 10177 = fire/ambulance. 10111 = police. 112 from any mobile phone connects to emergency services.

questions.question: The most important safety rule about home dangers is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most important safety rule about home dangers?
options: Tell a grown-up about anything that looks dangerous — and never play with chemicals, medicines or fire
questions.expected: Tell a grown-up about anything that looks dangerous — and never play with chemicals, medicines or fire
questions.memo: Tell a grown-up about anything that looks dangerous. Never play with chemicals, medicines or fire.

questions.question: You should always wear a seatbelt when you travel in a car.
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the picture. True or false: you should always wear a seatbelt in a car?
questions.context: Picture: a car seatbelt with its buckle.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: True. A seatbelt holds you safely in your seat and protects you if the car stops suddenly or crashes.

questions.question: What is the safest place to cross a busy road?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the picture. Where is the safest place to cross a busy road?
questions.context: Picture: a painted zebra crossing across a road.
options: In the middle of the road
Anywhere, as long as you run
questions.expected: At a zebra crossing
questions.memo: A zebra crossing is marked for people to cross, and drivers must stop for you. Crossing between cars or running across is dangerous.

LS.L5.PSW.T11.title: Water as an important basic need
LS.L5.PSW.T11.description: Importance of water, different ways of saving water, protecting the quality of water.
LS.L5.PSW.T11.recovery_strategy: Connect water lessons to SA reality — droughts, dams, taps. Small habits add up; the learner can really make a difference.

questions.question: Why is water important to life?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is water so important to life?
options: All living things — people, animals, plants — need water to survive
questions.expected: All living things — people, animals, plants — need water to survive
questions.memo: All living things need water to survive: people, animals and plants.

questions.question: About how much of a person's body is water?
questions.ruby_prompt: About how much of a person's body is water?
questions.expected: About 60%
questions.memo: Roughly 60% of our body weight is water. Children are a bit more — closer to 65%. That's why we feel ill so quickly when dehydrated.

questions.question: Which is a way to SAVE water at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to save water at home?
options: Take shorter showers and turn the tap off while brushing teeth
Wash one cup in lots of water
Water the garden in the hot midday sun
questions.expected: Take shorter showers and turn the tap off while brushing teeth
questions.memo: Small habits save a lot — a tap left on uses up to 9 litres a minute. Off when not in use = serious savings.

questions.question: True or false: South Africa is a water-scarce country.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: South Africa is a water-scarce country.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — SA is one of the 30 most water-scarce countries. We get less rain than many countries. Saving water is a national habit.

questions.question: Which is a way to PROTECT water quality?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to protect water quality?
options: Don't throw rubbish or chemicals into rivers, dams or drains
Wash motor parts in the river
questions.expected: Don't throw rubbish or chemicals into rivers, dams or drains
questions.memo: What goes in the drain often ends up in our water. Keep chemicals and rubbish OUT — and use proper bins and waste sites.

questions.question: What can polluted water cause?
questions.ruby_prompt: What can polluted water cause?
options: Serious illnesses like diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid
questions.expected: Serious illnesses like diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid
questions.memo: Dirty water kills millions of people worldwide each year. Diarrhoea, cholera, typhoid — all from water that wasn't clean.

questions.question: If you're not sure if water is clean, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: If you're not sure if water is clean to drink, you should:
options: Boil it for at least 1 minute before drinking
questions.expected: Boil it for at least 1 minute before drinking
questions.memo: Boil water for at least 1 minute. That kills most germs.

questions.question: Lerato leaves the tap running while brushing her teeth. About how much water can she waste in 2 minutes?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato leaves the tap running while she brushes for 2 minutes. About how much water can she waste?
questions.expected: Up to 18 litres
questions.memo: A running tap uses about 9 litres a minute. Turning it off saves nearly 20 litres per brush — many times a day.

questions.question: True or false: A small leak that drips can waste hundreds of litres a month.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: A small leak that drips can waste hundreds of litres a month.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — a slow drip can waste over 100 litres a month. Many drips across many homes = a huge loss. Fix leaks fast.

questions.question: Which household activity uses the MOST water?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which everyday activity at home uses the most water?
questions.expected: Bathing or showering
questions.memo: Showers and baths are the big water-users. A short shower beats a bath, and beats a long shower.

questions.question: Sipho's family is collecting rainwater in a tank. This helps because:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's family is collecting rainwater in a tank. Why is this helpful?
options: It reduces how much tap water they need for gardens or cleaning
questions.expected: It reduces how much tap water they need for gardens or cleaning
questions.memo: Rainwater harvesting is a smart SA habit — collected from the roof, stored in a tank, used for garden or cleaning. Saves municipal water.

questions.question: Put these in order for cleaning unsafe water in an emergency.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for cleaning unsafe water in an emergency.
options: Filter out big bits through a cloth
Boil the water for at least 1 minute
Store it in a clean covered container
questions.expected: Filter out big bits through a cloth,Boil the water for at least 1 minute,Let it cool,Store it in a clean covered container
questions.memo: Filter (removes dirt), boil (kills germs), cool, store covered. This sequence saves lives in floods, droughts and outages.

questions.question: Karabo's town goes on water restrictions during a drought. The community should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's town is on water restrictions because of a drought. What should the community do?
options: Follow the rules — short showers, no hosepipes, full washing loads only
Use even more water to be safe
questions.expected: Follow the rules — short showers, no hosepipes, full washing loads only
questions.memo: Follow the water rules: short showers, no hosepipes, full washing loads only. That protects everyone's share.

questions.question: Why are wetlands important for water?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are wetlands — marshy land near rivers — important for water?
options: They filter water naturally and store it
questions.expected: They filter water naturally and store it
questions.memo: Wetlands are nature's water filters — plants and soil clean the water as it passes through. Protecting wetlands = cleaner rivers.

questions.question: True or false: Washing a car with a bucket uses less water than a hosepipe.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Washing a car with a bucket uses less water than a hosepipe.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — a hosepipe runs free; a bucket uses just what's in it. Bucket wins on water saving every time.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you can do to save water.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one thing you can do to save water.
questions.expected: Turn off the tap while brushing teeth
questions.memo: Turn off the tap while you brush your teeth. Short showers and fixing leaks save water too.

questions.question: Why is water called a 'basic need'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do we call water a 'basic need'?
options: Without water, humans can survive only a few days — so it's essential, not optional
questions.expected: Without water, humans can survive only a few days — so it's essential, not optional
questions.memo: We can live weeks without food, but only days without water. Basic needs = things life cannot continue without.

questions.question: Mpho sees a cracked pipe leaking water into the street. She should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho sees a cracked pipe leaking water into the street. She should:
options: Tell a parent or report it to the municipality so it can be fixed
questions.expected: Tell a parent or report it to the municipality so it can be fixed
questions.memo: Tell a parent or report it to the municipality. A burst pipe wastes lots of clean water.

questions.question: Which is BEST for the environment when watering a garden?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's best for the environment when watering a garden?
options: Water early morning or evening, with grey water or a bucket if possible
Water at midday in full sun
questions.expected: Water early morning or evening, with grey water or a bucket if possible
questions.memo: Midday water evaporates before plants drink it. Early or late is efficient. Grey water (used bath/dishwater) is great for hardy plants.

questions.question: The most important truth about water in SA is:
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most important truth about water in South Africa?
options: It's precious and shared — every drop saved helps the whole community
questions.expected: It's precious and shared — every drop saved helps the whole community
questions.memo: Water is precious and shared. Every drop saved helps the whole community.

LS.L5.PSW.T12.title: Healthy eating for children
LS.L5.PSW.T12.description: South African Food-Based Dietary Guidelines, dietary needs of children, factors influencing food intake.
LS.L5.PSW.T12.recovery_strategy: Stay non-judgmental about favourite foods. Healthy = mostly good choices + room for treats. Frame food positively, not as 'good vs bad'.

questions.question: Which is the BIGGEST food group children should eat?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which food group should children eat the MOST of?
options: Starchy foods like pap, rice, bread, samp, potatoes
questions.expected: Starchy foods like pap, rice, bread, samp, potatoes
questions.memo: Starchy foods are the SA Dietary Guidelines' base — they give energy. Whole grains (brown bread, brown rice) are best.

questions.question: Which food group helps your body grow and repair?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which food group helps your body grow and repair itself?
options: Proteins — meat, fish, eggs, beans, peas, lentils, milk
questions.expected: Proteins — meat, fish, eggs, beans, peas, lentils, milk
questions.memo: Protein foods, like meat, eggs, beans and milk, help your body grow and heal.

questions.question: Why do we need fruit and vegetables every day?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do we need fruit and vegetables every day?
options: They give us vitamins, minerals and fibre that protect health
They make us taller in one day
questions.expected: They give us vitamins, minerals and fibre that protect health
questions.memo: Fruit and vegetables give us vitamins and fibre that keep us healthy.

questions.question: True or false: Eating too much sugar can lead to tooth decay and other health problems.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Eating too much sugar can lead to tooth decay and other health problems.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Too much sugar can cause holes in your teeth and other health problems.

questions.question: Which drink is BEST for everyday thirst?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which drink is best for everyday thirst?
questions.expected: Plain water
questions.memo: Plain water is best for thirst. It has no sugar.

questions.question: Which factor INFLUENCES what children eat?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which factor often influences what children eat?
options: What's available at home, school and shop, plus what parents and friends eat
Only the colour of the food
Only the day of the week
questions.expected: What's available at home, school and shop, plus what parents and friends eat
questions.memo: What's around us shapes our diet — at home, at school, in our community. Knowing this helps us choose more wisely.

questions.question: Sipho often skips breakfast. The most common effect is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho often skips breakfast. What's the most common effect?
options: Tired, hungry and trouble concentrating in class
questions.expected: Tired, hungry and trouble concentrating in class
questions.memo: Breakfast = brain fuel. Without it, focus drops, energy drops, mood drops. Even a simple porridge or bread + spread helps.

questions.question: Which is a HEALTHY school lunch idea?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a healthy school lunch idea?
options: Sandwich with protein (peanut butter or egg or chicken) + fruit + water
questions.expected: Sandwich with protein (peanut butter or egg or chicken) + fruit + water
questions.memo: A sandwich with egg, chicken or peanut butter, plus a fruit and water, is a healthy lunch.

questions.question: Lerato has a peanut allergy. What should she do at the lunch table?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato has a peanut allergy. What should she do at the lunch table?
options: Check that food she shares doesn't contain peanuts and tell adults about her allergy
Eat peanut butter to test it
questions.expected: Check that food she shares doesn't contain peanuts and tell adults about her allergy
questions.memo: Lerato should check food has no peanuts and tell adults about her allergy. It could make her very sick.

questions.question: Which is a sign of being well-fed and healthy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a sign of being well-fed and healthy?
options: Steady energy through the day, healthy weight, growing as expected
questions.expected: Steady energy through the day, healthy weight, growing as expected
questions.memo: A well-fed child has energy for school, play and sleep. Doctors and nurses can also check growth on a chart at the clinic.

questions.question: Why is FIBRE important for children?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is fibre important for children?
options: Fibre helps your tummy work well and keeps you regular
questions.expected: Fibre helps your tummy work well and keeps you regular
questions.memo: Fibre is in fruit skins, vegetables, beans, and whole grains. It keeps your digestion working and you feeling full.

questions.question: True or false: ALL children grow at exactly the same speed.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: All children grow at exactly the same speed.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Children grow at different speeds. Good food, sleep and exercise help each child grow in their own way.

questions.question: Karabo's family can't afford much meat. What's a good protein alternative?
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's family can't afford much meat. What's a good protein alternative?
options: Beans, lentils, peanut butter and eggs — affordable and full of protein
questions.expected: Beans, lentils, peanut butter and eggs — affordable and full of protein
questions.memo: Beans, lentils, peanut butter and eggs are full of protein and cost less than meat.

questions.question: Mpho ate a big bowl of pap, vegetables and a small piece of chicken. Her meal:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho ate pap, vegetables and a small piece of chicken. How balanced is her meal?
options: Balanced — it has starch, vegetables and protein
questions.expected: Balanced — it has starch, vegetables and protein
questions.memo: Three of the four key groups — starch + veg + protein. Add a glass of water and a fruit later and it's a healthy day.

questions.question: Put these foods in order from HEALTHIEST to least healthy as a daily snack.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these foods in order, healthiest first, as a daily snack.
questions.expected: Apple,Plain biltong (in moderation),Sweet biscuit,Sweets
questions.memo: Fruit first. Lean protein next. Then less-bad treats. Then plain sugar. Daily ≠ always; treats are fine sometimes.

questions.question: Tell me a healthy meal you like.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me a healthy meal that you like to eat.
questions.expected: Pap with vegetables and chicken
questions.memo: Good answers: any meal with a starch + a protein + vegetables. SA examples: pap + stew, samp and beans + spinach, rice + curry + salad.

questions.question: Why do children need MORE food per kilo of body weight than adults?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do children sometimes need more food per kilogram of body weight than adults?
options: Children are growing and use a lot of energy for growth and activity
questions.expected: Children are growing and use a lot of energy for growth and activity
questions.memo: Growth + activity = high energy needs. That's why a small child can eat surprisingly large amounts and still be healthy.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT influence what children eat?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these does NOT influence what children eat?
options: The day of the week's number
questions.expected: The day of the week's number
questions.memo: Money, family, friends, ads, culture — all real influences. The day-number does not. Knowing influences helps us see why we choose what we do.

questions.question: True or false: It's okay to have a sweet treat sometimes, not every day.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It's okay to have a sweet treat sometimes, just not every day.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. A treat sometimes is fine. The key is not every day.

questions.question: What's the BIG idea of healthy eating?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the big idea of healthy eating?
options: Eat a variety of foods from all groups, mostly whole foods, with water as the main drink
questions.expected: Eat a variety of foods from all groups, mostly whole foods, with water as the main drink
questions.memo: Variety + balance + water. That's the heart of the SA Dietary Guidelines. Whole foods over packaged ones, most of the time.

questions.question: Energy drinks are a healthy choice for children to drink every day.
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the picture. True or false: energy drinks are a healthy daily drink for children?
questions.context: Picture: a can of energy drink.
questions.expected: False
questions.memo: False. Energy drinks have a lot of sugar and caffeine, which are not healthy for children. Water is the best everyday drink.

LS.L5.PSW.T13.title: Local environmental health problems
LS.L5.PSW.T13.description: Locally occurring health problems (tuberculosis, diarrhoea, malaria, measles etc.) — causes, symptoms, available treatment.
LS.L5.PSW.T13.recovery_strategy: Focus on prevention and where to get help. SA has free public clinics and well-known prevention practices — keep tone hopeful and practical.

questions.question: What is TUBERCULOSIS (TB)?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is tuberculosis — TB?
options: A serious lung disease caused by germs (bacteria) that spreads through coughing
questions.expected: A serious lung disease caused by germs (bacteria) that spreads through coughing
questions.memo: TB attacks the lungs and spreads through the air when an infected person coughs. SA has one of the highest TB rates in the world.

questions.question: What is the main symptom of TB?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the main symptom of TB?
options: A cough that lasts more than 2 weeks, often with night sweats and weight loss
questions.expected: A cough that lasts more than 2 weeks, often with night sweats and weight loss
questions.memo: Long cough + night sweats + weight loss = see a clinic. TB is curable with the right medicine — but you have to start.

questions.question: Is TB curable?
questions.ruby_prompt: Is TB curable?
options: Yes — with the right medicine taken every day for 6 months, free at SA clinics
questions.expected: Yes — with the right medicine taken every day for 6 months, free at SA clinics
questions.memo: TB is curable. SA clinics give the medicine for free. Taking it every single day for the full course is critical.

questions.question: What causes most cases of DIARRHOEA in children?
questions.ruby_prompt: What causes most cases of diarrhoea in children?
options: Germs from dirty water or unwashed hands
questions.expected: Germs from dirty water or unwashed hands
questions.memo: Diarrhoea spreads through the mouth — from dirty water, food, or hands. Washing hands and clean water prevent most cases.

questions.question: What is the main treatment for diarrhoea in children?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the main treatment for diarrhoea in children?
options: Plenty of fluids and an oral rehydration solution (ORS)
questions.expected: Plenty of fluids and an oral rehydration solution (ORS)
questions.memo: Diarrhoea drains water and salts from the body. ORS sachets (free at clinics) replace them and save lives.

questions.question: What spreads MALARIA?
questions.ruby_prompt: What spreads malaria?
questions.context: Pictures: a mosquito, an apple, a drop of water, a handshake.
options: The bite of a specific kind of mosquito
questions.expected: The bite of a specific kind of mosquito
questions.memo: Malaria spreads through the bite of a certain kind of mosquito, mostly in the warm, low parts of the north-east.

questions.question: Which is a way to PREVENT malaria?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to prevent malaria?
options: Sleep under a mosquito net and use repellent in malaria areas
questions.expected: Sleep under a mosquito net and use repellent in malaria areas
questions.memo: In malaria areas, sleep under a mosquito net and use bug spray. They stop most bites.

questions.question: What is MEASLES?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is measles?
options: A serious viral disease that causes a fever and a red rash, especially in children
questions.expected: A serious viral disease that causes a fever and a red rash, especially in children
questions.memo: Measles is a serious sickness that causes a fever and a red rash, mostly in children. A vaccine protects against it.

questions.question: Which prevents measles?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which prevents measles?
options: The measles vaccine (given as part of the EPI — Expanded Programme on Immunisation)
questions.expected: The measles vaccine (given as part of the EPI — Expanded Programme on Immunisation)
questions.memo: The measles vaccine, given to all SA children for free, prevents measles. Catch-up vaccines are also free for older children who missed them.

questions.question: True or false: Vaccines protect children from many dangerous diseases.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Vaccines protect children from many dangerous diseases.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Vaccines have saved millions of children's lives. SA's free public vaccine programme covers measles, TB, polio, hepatitis and more.

questions.question: Where can you get free vaccines in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where can you get free vaccines in South Africa?
options: Only one hospital in the country
questions.expected: Any government clinic
questions.memo: Every government clinic gives vaccines for free. Your Road to Health booklet records them.

questions.question: Sipho's friend has a cough that won't go away after 3 weeks. He should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's friend has had a cough that won't go away for 3 weeks. What should he do?
options: See a clinic — a long cough could be TB and needs testing
questions.expected: See a clinic — a long cough could be TB and needs testing
questions.memo: Two-plus weeks of coughing is a red flag for TB. Clinics test for free. Early treatment saves lives and stops spread.

questions.question: Which is a way to prevent diarrhoea in a family?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to prevent diarrhoea in a family?
options: Wash hands, drink clean water, cook food well, cover food
questions.expected: Wash hands, drink clean water, cook food well, cover food
questions.memo: Four habits prevent most cases. They're simple, free and effective.

questions.question: Karabo's baby brother has bad diarrhoea for 2 days. The family should:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's baby brother has bad diarrhoea for 2 days. What should the family do?
options: Take him to the clinic urgently — babies dehydrate fast and need ORS
questions.expected: Take him to the clinic urgently — babies dehydrate fast and need ORS
questions.memo: Babies and small children dehydrate dangerously fast. Diarrhoea in babies = clinic now. ORS often saves the day.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for going to the clinic when you feel sick.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for going to the clinic when you feel sick.
options: Notice the symptoms (cough, fever, rash, diarrhoea)
Tell a parent or trusted adult
Take any medicine exactly as told
questions.expected: Notice the symptoms (cough, fever, rash, diarrhoea),Tell a parent or trusted adult,Visit the local clinic,Take any medicine exactly as told
questions.memo: Notice how you feel. Tell a parent or trusted adult. Go to the clinic. Take your medicine exactly as you are told.

questions.question: True or false: TB can be passed by sharing a meal with someone (eating from the same plate).
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: TB can be passed by sharing a meal from the same plate.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: TB spreads through the AIR (coughing, sneezing), not through food. Sharing food doesn't spread TB. (Wash hands anyway — for other reasons.)

questions.question: Why is COVERING YOUR MOUTH when coughing important?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is covering your mouth when coughing important?
options: It stops you from spreading germs to others
questions.expected: It stops you from spreading germs to others
questions.memo: Cough into your elbow (not hands — they spread germs to door handles, food). Saves others from your cold/flu/TB.

questions.question: Tell me one disease and one way to prevent it.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one disease and one way to prevent it.
questions.expected: Diarrhoea — wash hands before eating
questions.memo: Diarrhoea can be prevented by washing hands and drinking clean water. Malaria by mosquito nets. Measles by a vaccine.

questions.question: Mpho's family doesn't have clean drinking water. The safest thing to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho's family doesn't have clean drinking water. The safest thing to do is:
options: Boil all water for at least 1 minute or use water-purification tablets from a clinic
questions.expected: Boil all water for at least 1 minute or use water-purification tablets from a clinic
questions.memo: Boil all the water for at least 1 minute, or use water-cleaning tablets from a clinic.

questions.question: What's the most important thing to know about local health problems?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most important thing to know about local health problems?
options: Most can be prevented or treated — early help at a clinic saves lives
questions.expected: Most can be prevented or treated — early help at a clinic saves lives
questions.memo: Prevention + early treatment = the SA public health story. Free clinics, free vaccines, free TB medicine — use them, share them.

questions.question: Why should we never throw litter into a stormwater drain?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the picture of the drain. Why should we never throw litter into it?
questions.context: Picture: a street stormwater drain.
options: It blocks the drain and causes flooding and water pollution
It helps the water flow faster
It feeds the fish in the river
It makes the street look better
questions.expected: It blocks the drain and causes flooding and water pollution
questions.memo: Litter blocks the drain. Then the street floods when it rains, and the rubbish pollutes the river.

LS.L5.PSW.T14.title: HIV and AIDS: dealing with stigma
LS.L5.PSW.T14.description: Stigma about HIV and AIDS; how to change attitudes towards people infected with HIV and AIDS.
LS.L5.PSW.T14.recovery_strategy: Lead with facts; correct myths gently, not shamefully. Reinforce: HIV is a virus, not a moral failing. People with HIV deserve full friendship and dignity.

questions.question: What is 'stigma'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does the word 'stigma' mean?
options: When people are unfairly judged or shunned because of something about them
questions.expected: When people are unfairly judged or shunned because of something about them
questions.memo: Stigma is when people are unfairly judged or left out because of something about them, like an illness.

questions.question: Stigma around HIV often comes from:
questions.ruby_prompt: Stigma around HIV often comes from what?
options: Old myths, fear, and lack of accurate information
questions.expected: Old myths, fear, and lack of accurate information
questions.memo: When people don't know how HIV actually spreads, fear fills the gap with myths. Real information ends stigma.

questions.question: True or false: People with HIV are NORMAL people who happen to have a virus.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: People with HIV are normal people who happen to have a virus.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. HIV is a virus — like flu or measles, only specific in how it spreads. Having it doesn't change who someone is as a person.

questions.question: A student with HIV joins your class. The right attitude is:
questions.ruby_prompt: A new classmate with HIV joins your class. What's the right attitude?
options: Welcome them like any other classmate — they can't infect you in everyday school life
questions.expected: Welcome them like any other classmate — they can't infect you in everyday school life
questions.memo: HIV doesn't spread through everyday school life — sharing pencils, food, desks, hugs, sport. Welcoming them is right AND safe.

questions.question: Stigma can affect a person with HIV by:
questions.ruby_prompt: Stigma can affect a person with HIV by:
options: Making them afraid to get tested or take medicine — which makes them sicker
questions.expected: Making them afraid to get tested or take medicine — which makes them sicker
